# Replicate & Test Guides — high level of task interruptions

Task `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of
interruptions"). Companion to `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` (the wide-net cause
analysis). This folder turns each hypothesis from that analysis into a quick
guide: **how to recognise it, how to replicate or test it, and what is safe
to run versus what needs explicit permission first.**

Screenshot reference: `assets/image.png` — task `7f6220c3` showing repeated
"Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and inflated
"Tried N times" badges (Merge resolver x6, Quick review x6, Automated tests
x10, In Progress x11).

Scope note: this stage is **docs-only**. Every test below is a markdown
snippet for a follow-up code stage; no source or test files were added to the
repo. Run commands assume `node_modules` is installed (`npm install` in
`api/` and `frontend/`; runner tests need only Node's built-in runner).

## Safety tiers used in every guide

| Tier | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **SAFE-LOCAL** | Runs entirely on this machine against temp dirs, in-memory Fastify (`app.inject`), or mock stores. No prod data, no agents, no network beyond localhost. | Unit tests for the ledger, scheduler, runner workdir cap, git-hook failure, 413 body limit |
| **PROD-READ-ONLY** | Reads production state (backend API `192.168.1.206:3100`, runner journals on the backend host or server2, worktrees `kb-<taskId>`). No writes, but still prod access. | Fleet-wide history recount, journal greps, worktree forensics |
| **PROD-ACTION** | Anything that invokes a real agent stage, restarts a runner/backend, reaps worktrees, or mutates task state. | Re-running `7f6220c3`'s Merge resolver, restarting `local-alpha`, manual resume of parked tasks |

**Rule for this task:** SAFE-LOCAL guides may be run freely. Anything marked
PROD-READ-ONLY or PROD-ACTION is documented as a *procedure only* — **do not
execute it without explicit user permission**. Each such section is marked
`PROD-ONLY — DO NOT RUN WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION`.

## Verdict table (cause -> guide -> replicability)

| # | Cause (from WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md) | Guide | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worktree-cap exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap 5) | `GUIDE-01-worktree-cap-loop.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (runner `node:test` + api vitest) |
| 2 | HTTP 413 on `complete-execution` (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default) | `GUIDE-02-413-complete-payload.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (Fastify `inject`); real-task confirmation is PROD-READ-ONLY |
| 3 | local-alpha setup-phase deaths (bare, ~5 s, no `prompted`) | `GUIDE-03-local-alpha-setup-deaths.md` | PARTIAL locally (backend side simulatable); root cause PROD-READ-ONLY on the local-alpha host |
| 4 | Backend-unreachable / 502 crashing the daemon mid-run | `GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (localhost mock backend returning 502 / dropping); window-joining is PROD-READ-ONLY |
| 5 | Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks) | `GUIDE-05-commit-push-crash-loop.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (temp git repo + failing hook); real agent e2e is PROD-ACTION |
| 6 | Backend server restarts orphaning `running_*` tasks | `GUIDE-06-backend-restart-orphans.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (mock-store unit test of `reconcileInterruptedRuns`); fleet check PROD-READ-ONLY. Analysis: 0 occurrences observed — monitor only |
| A | Amplifier: Rule-0 instant re-dispatch, death counter counts cap refusals, "Tried N times" and the "after server restart" label | `GUIDE-07-amplifier-requeue-and-display.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (api + frontend unit tests) |
| T | Consolidated copy-paste test recipes and exact run commands | `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` | Reference |

## How to read a guide

Each guide has the same sections:

1. **Signature** — what the flake looks like in the UI / task history / journals.
2. **Replicability verdict** — one of REPLICABLE-LOCALLY / PARTIAL / PROD-ONLY.
3. **Safe local replication** — steps + a TDD-style test example (red test first,
   then the code path that should satisfy it).
4. **Prod-only verification** (if any) — the exact commands that *would* be
   run on prod, clearly flagged, not to be executed without explicit user
   permission.
5. **Evidence to collect** — what to save if the issue is reproduced.

## Test-run commands used throughout

```bash
# api unit tests (vitest), from repo root:
cd api && npx vitest run flow/executionLedger.test.js        # single file
npm run test:api                                            # whole api suite

# frontend unit tests (vitest):
cd frontend && npx vitest run src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js

# runner unit tests (node:test, no deps beyond Node >= 20):
node --test runner/project.test.js
node --test runner/daemon.test.js
```

New test files for these guides are **not** added in this docs-only stage;
`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` says exactly where each snippet would live. Note the
repo gate pins every `runner/*.test.js` in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`
(`buildBranches`), so a new runner suite file must also be registered there
in the code stage.

# RESPONSE — follow-up solutions for "high level of interruptions"

Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: triage of `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` + replication guides into
reviewable, parallelisable follow-up tasks.

Inputs reviewed: `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` (6 causes + amplifier, 118 interrupts surveyed
across 61 tasks in project `0fd41821`), `REPLICATION-INDEX.md`, `GUIDE-01`–`GUIDE-07`,
`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, and `assets/image.png` (task `7f6220c3` timeline showing repeated
"Auto-resumed after server restart" rows and inflated "Tried N times" badges).
Key code seams were spot-checked in the repo (`executionLedger.js`,
`autoResumeTask.js`, `daemon.js` cap branch, `project.js` cap refusal) and match the
analysis. No prod commands were run; all prod procedures below are quoted from the
guides as procedures for a later permitted step.

## Triage verdict: what is worth tackling

| Cause (per WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS) | Evidence strength | Tackle? | Solution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Worktree-cap exhaustion loop (49/118, reason-proven) | high | **Yes** | S1: stop counting cap refusals as deaths + add re-dispatch backoff |
| 2. HTTP 413 on `complete-execution` (5 proven, ≤15 suspected) | high (proven case) | **Yes** | S2: raise/shrink the completion payload + never crash-loop on 413 |
| 3. local-alpha setup-phase deaths (~60 bare/fast, fault unnamed) | medium (localised, root unknown) | **Yes, investigate first** | S3: prod-journal investigation (E1/E6), then a targeted fix from findings |
| 4. Backend-unreachable/502 crashing daemon mid-run | medium-low | **Yes** | S4: non-fatal transient backend errors in-assignment |
| 5. Commit/push crash loop | medium (fix `046a6391` already merged 11-21, needs rollout) | **Rollout + verify, no new code yet** | S5 (with S6); new code only if E5 finds uncovered cases |
| 6. Backend restarts orphaning tasks (0/118) | high (ruled out) | **No — monitor only** | S7: one regression-pin test + recount; no behaviour change |
| Amplifier: instant Rule-0 re-dispatch, death-counter misuse, "Tried N" inflation, "server restart" mislabel | high (confirmed mechanics) | **Yes — cheapest wins** | S1 (counter/backoff) + S6 (display fixes) |
| Cross-cutting | — | **Yes** | S5: 0.2.x runner rollout + fleet before/after recount |

Dropped / deferred: nothing is dropped outright except Cause 6 as an active fix
(zero occurrences; monitor-only). Cause 3 gets an investigation task rather than a
fix task because any fix written before E1 (local-alpha journal) would be guessing.

Coordination note: task `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit
hooks") has an `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` that touches the same `executeAssignment`
generic-catch containment area as S4. Whoever picks up S4 must read that plan first
and either build on it or explicitly scope against it to avoid duplicate/overlapping
daemon-catch changes. Likewise S5-verify covers the rollout of the `1cae113f` fix
(`046a6391`); do not re-implement deterministic-git-failure handling.

## Blocking / parallelism map

```
S1 (backend counter+backoff) ──────────────┐
S2 (413 payload) ──────────────────────────┤  all parallel,
S4 (daemon transient tolerance) ───────────┤  no code dependencies
S6 (display labels/counts) ────────────────┤  between them
S7 (reconcile regression pin) ─────────────┘
S3 (local-alpha journal investigation) ──blocks──> S3b (targeted setup fix, TBD from findings)
S5 (0.2.x rollout + recount) ──enables──> reason-based confirmation for S3/S4
                                           (code work proceeds in parallel; only the
                                           *prod confirmation* of S3/S4 waits on S5)
```

Recommended creation order (all can then run in parallel): S1, S2, S6, S7, S3, S5, S4.
Immediate relief comes from S1 (backend-only, no runner rollout needed) and S2-backend.

Global before/after metric for every solution: the fleet-count script in
`GUIDE-07 §5` (runner_interrupts / with_reason / auto_resumed / server_restart /
escalated per task) plus the `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2` table, re-run after each fix
rolls out. A fix has worked when its signature row drops and nothing else rises.

---

## S1 — Cap refusals must not count as runner deaths; add re-dispatch backoff (backend-only)

**Answers Cause 1 + part of the amplifier.** All 49 reasoned interrupts are
`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals, yet `interruptExecution` increments
`runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally, so five capacity refusals park the task as a
`runner-death-loop` (42 escalations fleet-wide). And every interrupt re-dispatches
in ~150 ms with Rule-0 priority, so the same still-full runner re-claims instantly.

**Proposed change (backend, `api/`):**
1. In `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution`: do not increment
   `runnerInterruptCount` (and do not escalate) when the reason indicates graceful
   capacity refusal — i.e. reason starts with `Runner workdir unavailable:`.
   Record the refusal in history as today (keep the reason string; it is the
   detector), but track it on a separate counter (e.g. `capacityRefusalCount`)
   with its own operator-visibility threshold rather than the death bound.
2. In the scheduler (`api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js` / `findResumedCandidate.js`):
   add backoff for repeatedly resumed tasks — e.g. after N consecutive resumes of the
   same task+stage, delay re-dispatch (bootstrapped small, e.g. 30 s → 5 min) and/or
   sort behind fresh work, and prefer dispatch to a *different* runner than the one
   that just refused. Keep the first resume fast (today's behaviour) so genuine
   one-off flakes still recover instantly.
3. Keep `isAutoResumableWithReason.js` `runner-death-loop` parking for true death
   streaks (crashes with no capacity reason).

**Tests (from `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` / GUIDE-01 + GUIDE-07):**
- Red: `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` — five cap-reason
  interrupts leave `runnerInterruptCount` at 0, no `runner-death-loop` park.
- Red: `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` — after N
  consecutive resumes, fresh work wins over the flapping task.
- Keep a pin: five *bare/crash* interrupts still park (existing behaviour in
  `executionLedger.test.js` around line 778 must keep passing).

**How to confirm the bug (before writing the fix):**
- Local (SAFE-LOCAL): run the GUIDE-01 §3 backend snippet — it demonstrates five
  cap refusals parking as `runner-death-loop` on current code.
- Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): `GET /tasks/<id>` on `350ca162`,
  `db24c124`, `7b69d365` — confirm cap-reason strings followed by `Runner deaths
  escalated` at count 5. After the fix + deploy (backend-only, no runner rollout):
  re-run the same histories on new interrupts and the GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script —
  `escalated` should drop while `with_reason` stays visible.

**Parallel/blocking:** none. Backend-only; safe to ship first.
**Risk:** low-medium. Touching the escalation rule changes parking behaviour — the
pin tests above are the guard. Smallest safe slice is the counter exclusion alone;
backoff can be a second commit in the same task if review prefers.

## S2 — Fix the 413 completion-payload loop (backend limit + runner payload + no crash on 413)

**Answers Cause 2 (proven: 5 crash-loop laps on `7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 11-20
21:19–21:47, restart counters 830→834).** After a fully successful run + push, the
`complete-execution` POST exceeds Fastify's default 1 MiB JSON body limit
(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`) and is rejected with 413; the daemon's
generic catch interrupts (bare on 0.1.0) and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart →
full stage re-run → same 413. Deterministic, burns a whole run per lap.

**Proposed change (both sides; either half alone breaks the loop, both together
remove the class):**
1. Backend: set an explicit `bodyLimit` for the runner `complete-execution` route
   (raise to a deliberate value, e.g. 10 MiB — document why, do not just copy the
   accessibility route's value without checking it) and log rejected oversize
   bodies with task id + byte size so the next 413 is diagnosable from backend
   logs instead of invisible (today the backend rejects before routing and leaves
   no task-history trace).
2. Runner: shrink `collectTaskFiles` (`runner/daemon.js:1820`) so the envelope
   cannot exceed the agreed limit — exclude binary assets (PNG screenshots) or
   downsample the file set, and account for `output` (20 KiB) + JSON overhead in
   the cumulative cap rather than capping the files array at 1 MiB and then adding
   the envelope on top.
3. Runner: treat HTTP 413 from `complete-execution` as a deterministic,
   non-retryable completion failure (report once as failed with the size details,
   return — never rethrow). A 413 is proof the stage ran fine and only the report
   was too big; it must never become an interrupt + restart.

**Tests:**
- Pin (passes today): `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` + `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js`
  (GUIDE-02 §2) — then flip to assert the new explicit limit after the change.
- `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` (GUIDE-02 §3) — many sub-256 KiB files +
  output + envelope must stay under the agreed limit.
- Daemon-level: stubbed `client.complete` throwing a 413-shaped error → failed
  completion recorded, no interrupt, no rethrow (mirror the GUIDE-04 §3 shape).

**How to confirm the bug:**
- Local (SAFE-LOCAL): the GUIDE-02 §2 `app.inject` test proves >1 MiB bodies get
  413 on current wiring; the §3 test proves the file+envelope composition exceeds it.
- Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): backend access log 11-20 21:15–21:47 for
  the five 413s + sizes (E2); `Backend 413` sweep on both runner journals (E3);
  `kb-7f6220c3` worktree shows pushed stage-output commits for the looped executions
  (do NOT reap that worktree — it is the exhibit). After fix: no new `Backend 413`
  lines; any future oversize report surfaces as a failed completion with size details.

**Parallel/blocking:** none on other solutions. Internal order: backend limit raise
can ship before the runner payload shrink (backend deploys immediately; runner needs
rollout). Coordinate the agreed limit value between the two halves in the task's plan.
**Risk:** low. Raising a body limit is safe; the runner shrink must keep task-docs
sync useful (assert the kept-file set in tests).

## S3 — Investigate the local-alpha setup-phase deaths (evidence task, then targeted fix)

**Answers Cause 3 — the volume-dominant signature (96/118 local-alpha, 99/118 ≤15 s
after `started`, median 4.7 s, no `prompted`).** The fault is localised to
`prepareWorkdir` but genuinely unnamed, because deployed 0.1.0 attaches no reason on
the generic path. Writing a fix now would be guessing.

**Proposed task shape — strict two-phase, investigation first:**
1. Phase A (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs explicit permission + backend-host access):
   collect E1 — local-alpha daemon journal on `192.168.1.206` (user `server`) for
   the exhibit windows (`c5c465c4` 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` 11-20 15:38–15:43,
   18:39–18:41, 11-21 10:16 + 13:34): the `Runner failed: <message>` lines name the
   fault, restart-counter deltas separate crash-loops from in-process re-claim loops.
   Also E6: runner build provenance via `GET /runners`, plus work-root/disk/git-mirror
   health on the backend host at those times. Exact commands are in GUIDE-03 §4.
2. Phase B: write the targeted fix from whatever Phase A names (likely candidates:
   git lock/fetch/push-race handling, docs-worktree handling — note `7f6220c3` IS the
   separate-docs-repo task — stale mirror, disk/permissions). If Phase A is
   inconclusive, the fallback deliverable is defined hardening, not a shrug:
   per-step timing + error capture inside `prepareWorkdir` so the next occurrence
   self-diagnoses, plus the generic S4 containment below.
3. Cheap parallel hardening that does NOT wait for Phase A (include in this task or
   S4, reviewer's call): assert/record the runner version on every interrupt history
   row so old-build bare interrupts stay attributable (GUIDE-03 §2 TDD angle).

**Tests:** GUIDE-03 §2 backend storm pin + `runner/project.setupFaults.test.js`
failure-shape pins (§3) are the regression floor. The Phase-B fix must add its own
red test reproducing the named fault in a temp work root.
**How to confirm the bug:** Phase A *is* the confirmation — a `Runner failed:`
message timestamp-joined to a `started` → bare-interrupt pair. Post-0.2.x-rollout
(S5), bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should name this cause directly;
re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
**Parallel/blocking:** Phase A is independent and can start immediately (needs access
permission, not code). Phase B (S3b) is the only task in this response blocked on
another task's output. Prod *confirmation* of the fix waits on the S5 rollout.
**Risk:** low (read-only) for Phase A. Do not let Phase B expand into "rewrite
setup" — one named fault, one fix, one red test.

## S4 — Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal (daemon containment)

**Answers Cause 4 (501 `fetch failed` + 16 `Backend 502` since 11-19 on server2-alpha;
a proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).** Today any
in-`try` backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and
rethrows → process exit → systemd restart. Heartbeat failures are tolerated (lease
TTL) but in-assignment call failures are fatal, so every LAN blip or backend restart
window can kill a run.

**Proposed change (runner, `runner/daemon.js` + `runner/client.js`):**
1. In the `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2452`): transient backend
   errors (`fetch failed` network errors, 502/503/504 status) during an assignment
   send an interrupt *with reason* and **return** (keep polling) instead of rethrowing —
   the same report-and-return precedent as the existing `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and
   deterministic-`gitFailure` branches. Lease TTL already bounds the damage.
2. Add bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (heartbeat, dispatch poll)
   so the idle loop stops crash-cycling (restart counters 366→367 in the 11-19 sample)
   — or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit on those paths.
3. Keep fatal: `STALE_EPOCH` (epoch fencing must propagate), auth failures, and
   genuinely unknown errors — enumerate the non-fatal set explicitly (status codes +
   `fetch failed` cause) rather than inverting the catch-all, so new failure modes
   stay loud.

**Must-read before coding:** `docs/tasks/db49d6c6-*/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`
(runner recovery containment) — build on it or scope against it; do not land a
second competing catch-restructure.
**Tests:** `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (GUIDE-04 §2: 502 shape, dropped-socket
shape, recovery) + the §3 daemon fatality-boundary test flipped red
(`expect(rethrown).toBe(false)` for transient errors, still-true for stale-epoch).
Register any new `runner/*.test.js` in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (`buildBranches`).
**How to confirm the bug:** local — the §2/§3 tests fail-or-pin the fatality on current
code. Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): E4 timestamp-join of server2-alpha
`Runner failed: fetch failed|Backend 502` lines against `started` → interrupt pairs
on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`; E7 backend/proxy
availability log for 11-19 → 11-21. After rollout: crash-restart rate in the runner
journal drops while assignment success rate holds.
**Parallel/blocking:** code-independent of S1/S2/S6. Shares the daemon catch with the
`db49d6c6` work — sequence with that task, not with anything here.
**Risk:** medium. Changing fatal→non-fatal can mask real failures — the explicit
non-fatal enumeration + reason-on-interrupt + journal loudness are the guards.

## S5 — Roll out 0.2.x runners and run the fleet before/after recount (ops + verification)

**Covers Cause 5 verification and unlocks diagnosis of Causes 3–4.** Deployed runners
are 0.1.0 (main `f430f53`, 11-11); repo is 0.2.0 with interrupt reasons and
deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`).
Rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle-converge
(`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so lag is expected — but until it lands, every new
interrupt is still bare and every commit-hook rejection still crash-loops.

**Proposed steps:**
1. Confirm both runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge to the build
   containing `046a6391` per the runbook; record `GET /runners` versions before/after.
2. Re-run the `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2` counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script: bare
   interrupts should drop to ~0, reasons should name Causes 1/3/4 directly, and
   deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED completions with
   `gitFailure` payloads, never as interrupts.
3. Run the E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4): for each remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt, check `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`,
   `7f6220c3`) for stage-output-commit presence (present → Cause 2/4 territory;
   absent → Cause 5). Only if E5 finds commit-loop cases the `046a6391` fix does not
   cover should a new Cause-5 code task be created.
4. Record the post-rollout counts in the task folder as the new baseline for S1–S4.

**How to confirm the underlying bugs:** this task *is* the confirmation harness —
before/after counts plus the journal sweeps (E3 `Backend 413`, E4 502/fetch-fail,
E5 hook/commit lines). No new unit tests; deliverable is the recount + version record.
**Parallel/blocking:** runs in parallel with all code work; only prod *confirmation*
of S3/S4/S2-runner-half waits on it.
**Risk:** low. Follow the runbook; do not force-restart runners mid-assignment to
speed convergence (observe only — forced restarts are PROD-ACTION and risk new
interrupts, which is exactly what we are measuring).

## S6 — Fix the misleading display: resume label + "Tried N times" (backend + frontend)

**Answers the amplifier's display half — the cheapest, lowest-risk task, and the one
that fixes what the reporter actually saw.** `autoResumeTask` uses one history string
for both recovery routes, so 100 runner-path resumes display as "server restarts that
never happened" (0 recorded); `summarizeStageRuns` counts every `Resumed` row into
`tryCount`, producing the screenshot's ×6/×10/×11 badges.

**Proposed change:**
1. Backend (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`): distinct history strings per
   recovery route — keep `Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue`
   for genuine reconcile recoveries, add e.g. `Auto-resumed after runner interrupt —
   prioritised in queue` (include runner id + reason when present) for runner-path
   resumes. Use the existing `interruptedBy` marker to pick the route.
2. Frontend (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js` `summarizeStageRuns`,
   `:483-536`): exclude `Resumed` rows from `tryCount` (they are infra re-tries, not
   stage attempts) — or show them separately (e.g. `Tried 2 times · 4 infra resumes`).
   Update `formatTryCount` (`:556`) accordingly.
3. Update the existing pins that encode current behaviour (`taskFormatters.test.js`
   `summarizeStageRuns` cases, `taskScheduler.test.js:896` autoResume block,
   `stallRecovery`/`startupRecovery` integration tests referencing the label) —
   this is an intended contract change, not a regression; each updated assertion must
   state the new expected string/count explicitly.

**Tests:** `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` (GUIDE-07 §2 — pin-then-red),
frontend `summarizeStageRuns` pin-then-red (§4). Full gate: `npm run test:api`,
`npm run test:frontend`.
**How to confirm the bug:** local — the §2/§4 pin tests pass on current code, proving
the mislabel and the inflation; the red tests fail until fixed. Prod (read-only):
map `assets/image.png`-style rows to `GET /tasks/7f6220c3` history — Resumed rows
counted into badges, runner-path resumes labelled "server restart".
**Parallel/blocking:** fully independent. Good first task.
**Risk:** low. User-visible strings change — keep old-row rendering backward compatible
(histories already written keep the old string; only new resumes use the new one).

## S7 — Regression-pin the boot reconcile + keep Cause 6 ruled out (tiny backend test task)

**Cause 6 is ruled out (0/118, publish-only deploys, observed restart orphaned
nothing) — this task keeps it ruled out.** `reconcileInterruptedRuns` is the one path
that *should* write `interrupted by server restart`; pin it so future boot-order or
status-set changes are caught, and re-run the zero-count check after each deploy.

**Proposed change:** add `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js`
exactly as specified in GUIDE-06 §2 (orphan flip + history row, engine-owned task
untouched, idempotence, legacy `running_deploy` coverage). No behaviour change.
**How to confirm:** the tests pass immediately (PIN, not red). Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY):
the GUIDE-06 §4 loop — any `interrupted by server restart` row re-opens Cause 6.
**Parallel/blocking:** independent; can be folded into S1 or S6 if review prefers
fewer tasks, but kept separate here so it is never skipped.
**Risk:** negligible.

---

## Suggested review checklist (for the reviewing agent + human)

- [ ] Each task above names its files/seams, its red/pin tests with run commands,
  and both a local repro and a prod read-only confirmation — nothing ships on
  "looks right".
- [ ] S3 stays investigation-first: no Phase-B fix without a named fault from E1.
- [ ] S4 is sequenced with (not duplicated against) the `db49d6c6` containment work.
- [ ] S2's backend limit and runner payload cap agree on one number, documented.
- [ ] New `runner/*.test.js` files are registered in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`;
  new/renamed exports get `MARK:` JSDoc + `npm run check:jsdoc-example`.
- [ ] No PROD-READ-ONLY/PROD-ACTION command runs without explicit user permission;
  `kb-7f6220c3` is not reaped (2.8 MiB exhibit + pushed commits).
- [ ] S5's post-rollout recount is recorded as the baseline before S1–S4 claim victory.

# TDD Test Examples — consolidated recipes for the interruption flakes

All snippets are for a follow-up **code stage** (this stage is docs-only, so
no test files were added to the repo). Each recipe: red test first (it should
fail or pin current behaviour), then the code change that turns it green.
Full snippets live in the per-cause guides linked below; this file is the
map + run commands.

## Where each test would live and how to run it

| Guide | Proposed test file | Runner | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| GUIDE-01 cap loop | `runner/project.worktreeCap.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/project.worktreeCap.test.js` |
| GUIDE-01 backend | `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` |
| GUIDE-02 413 | `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js`, `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js bodyLimit.default.test.js` |
| GUIDE-02 payload | `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` |
| GUIDE-03 storm | `api/flow/scheduler/bareInterruptStorm.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/bareInterruptStorm.test.js` |
| GUIDE-03 setup faults | `runner/project.setupFaults.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/project.setupFaults.test.js` |
| GUIDE-04 outage | `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` |
| GUIDE-05 hook loop | `runner/gitOps.hookCrashLoop.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/gitOps.hookCrashLoop.test.js` |
| GUIDE-05 backend | `api/flow/executionLedger.commitLoop.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/executionLedger.commitLoop.test.js` |
| GUIDE-06 reconcile | `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` |
| GUIDE-07 label | `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` |
| GUIDE-07 priority | `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` |
| GUIDE-07 tryCount | additions to `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js` | vitest | `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js` |

Housekeeping for the code stage:

- New `runner/*.test.js` files MUST be added to the explicit list in
  `scripts/run-tests.mjs` `buildBranches()` ("Unit Tests (runner)") —
  `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins that every runner suite is registered.
- New/renamed exports in `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/` need a JSDoc
  block with `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example`; run
  `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1 s) before pushing.
- Full gate: `npm test` (or `npm test -- --no-canary` for a fast cycle);
  per-area: `npm run test:api`, `npm run test:frontend`.

## TDD workflow per issue

1. **Write the red test** from the guide (most are written to FAIL against
   current code — they encode the desired fix: cap refusals not counted as
   deaths, distinct resume label, Resumed rows excluded from tryCount,
   non-fatal transient backend errors, backoff on repeated resumes).
2. **Run it, confirm red.**
3. **Change the seam** named in the guide (`executionLedger.js`,
   `autoResumeTask.js`, `taskFormatters.js`, `daemon.js` catch, …).
4. **Run green**, then the full gate.
5. Tests that only PIN current behaviour (marked "PIN" in the guides, e.g.
   the 413 default, the reconcile flip) should pass immediately — they are
   regression guards, not red tests.

## What CANNOT be tested locally — do not attempt without explicit user permission

| Item | Why | Tier | Where documented |
|---|---|---|---|
| Root cause of local-alpha bare setup deaths | Deployed 0.1.0 attaches no reason; only the local-alpha host journal (192.168.1.206) names it | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-03 §4 (E1) |
| Fleet-wide interrupt recount / before-after 0.2.x rollout | Live backend API, project `0fd41821` | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-03 §4 (E6), GUIDE-07 §5 |
| 413 confirmation on real tasks (`7f6220c3`) + journal sweeps | Runner journals + backend access log on prod hosts | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-02 §4 (E2/E3) |
| Crash-vs-reclaim join for server2-alpha interrupts | server2 journal + task histories | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-04 §4 (E4) |
| Backend downtime window enumeration | backend/proxy logs on prod host | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-04 §4 (E7) |
| Worktree forensics on `kb-<taskId>` exhibits | Runner hosts; do NOT reap `kb-7f6220c3` | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-02 §4, GUIDE-05 §4 (E5) |
| Any re-run of a real agent stage (e.g. resuming parked `7f6220c3`) | Invokes a real agent against the live backend, burns a stage run, mutates task state | PROD-ACTION | GUIDE-03 §4 |
| Restarting/reaping prod runners or backend to force a repro | Mutates shared prod systems | PROD-ACTION | — (not recommended; observe only) |

None of the PROD-READ-ONLY / PROD-ACTION commands in the guides were
executed for this stage. They are procedures only — **run them only with
explicit user permission**.

## Safe local e2e option (no prod, still opt-in)

A full loop reproduction without touching prod is possible against a
**scratch stack**: `docker compose up` a dev backend on localhost, register a
local runner, create a scratch project, pre-fill the runner work root with 5
fresh `kb-*` dirs (Cause 1) or install a failing pre-commit hook in the
scratch project (Cause 5), then watch `GET /tasks/<id>` history. This still
invokes a real agent harness, so treat it as opt-in and time-boxed; the unit
recipes above cover the same mechanics without an agent.

reports.name: WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md
reports.content:
# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — high level of task interruptions

Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: DO research (investigatory only — no solutions proposed).

## 0. Inputs

- **Bug report**: many tasks end with interruptions suggesting flakiness; reporter
  notes a `local-alpha` runner restart-loop incident and wonders if it is related;
  interruptions "should happen rarely but they are seemingly quite common".
- **Screenshot** (`assets/image.png`): task `7f6220c3` ("add support for projects
  having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo") showing repeated
  "Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and high
  "Tried N times" counts (Merge resolver ×6, Quick review ×6, Automated
  tests ×10, In Progress ×11).
- **Survey result**: the Questionnaire stage recorded `Survey completed (none)` —
  the `question-me` skill requested no survey questions, so there is no
  `SURVEY.md` with human answers. All evidence below comes from repo code,
  the live backend API, runner worktrees, and the runner systemd journal.

## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)

Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):

1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
   an authenticated runner daemon.

Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).

## 2. Fleet-wide numbers (live backend, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21)

| Signal | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Runner-path interrupts (`interrupted execution`) | 118 | across 30/61 tasks (~half the project) |
| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |

Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.

Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle
converge (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so rollout lag is expected.

## 3. Possible causes

### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)

**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
suspected death loop.

**Pros (for).**
- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)
  carry `Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5); ...
  (every orphan was used recently, nothing stale to evict)`. Both hosts appear
  (`/home/server/.kainbain` = local-alpha host, `/home/server2/.kainbain` =
  server2-alpha host).
- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

**Cons (against).**
- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
  both hosts).
- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike
  (48 bare) needs a different driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `350ca162` (12 cap interrupts), `db24c124` (9), `7b69d365` (6), `3c12ffcd`
  (5), `f56e9878` (4), `1f8959ca` (5) — confirm each shows the cap reason and
  same-runner re-claim.
- Runner-side: work-root occupancy time series per host around 11-09 and
  11-16/17; orphan-staleness / LRU-eviction decisions in daemon logs.
- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
  cheapest ongoing detector (no host access needed).

### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)

**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`; the only explicit `bodyLimit` in the
API is the accessibility route).

**Pros (for).**
- Smoking gun in the server2-alpha journal (`journalctl --user
  -u kainbain-runner-server2-alpha`): on 11-20, five consecutive cycles of
  `Committed <sha> (pushed: true)` → `Runner failed: Backend 413 on
  /tasks/7f6220c3-.../complete-execution` → `Main process exited, status=1`
  → `Scheduled restart job, restart counter 830→834`, at 21:19, 21:29, 21:35,
  21:43, 21:47 — exactly matching the five `finished` → bare-interrupt pairs
  in task `7f6220c3` history.
- Worktree forensics agree: `kb-7f6220c3` holds the pushed stage-output commits
  with matching timestamps, and `origin` has them — proving failure happened
  strictly after push.
- Deterministic: same task files every lap → same 413 → loop only ends via the
  death-bound park (observed: parked at count 7).
- Explains why the newest, longest, most asset-heavy stages (Merge resolver
  with proof screenshots) interrupt while short stages complete.

**Cons (against).**
- Proven for exactly one task-stage so far (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 5
  interrupts); the other 10 post-`finished` bare interrupts are unexamined.
- Cannot explain the 99 sub-15s interrupts (413 only happens at completion,
  minutes in).
- Backend 413 leaves no task-history trace of its own (the backend rejects
  before routing), so backend history alone can never confirm/deny further
  cases — runner journals are required.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `7f6220c3` (screenshot task; Merge-resolver window 11-20 21:15–21:47):
  backend access/error log for the five 413s (confirm size vs limit);
  preserve `kb-7f6220c3` worktree (do not reap) — 2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit.
- Journal sweep on both runner hosts for `Backend 413` across all tasks/dates
  (server2-alpha: 5 hits since 11-19, all this task; local-alpha journal still
  needed — host `192.168.1.206`, user `server`).
- Any other task whose `finished` → interrupt gap is seconds with a preceding
  multi-minute run is a 413 suspect; check runner journals first, backend
  history second (it will be bare).

### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)

**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).

**Pros (for).**
- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
  11-20 (18).
- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
  (only uncaught fallible step there).
- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.

**Cons (against).**
- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
  restart counters are unknown from here.
- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`
  (12× local) — need the **local-alpha daemon journal on the backend host**
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`, systemd user unit) for those windows: the
  `Runner failed: <message>` line names the fault, and restart-counter lines
  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.
- local-alpha build provenance: confirm it is also pre-11-21 (expected bare);
  after the 0.2.x rollout, bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should
  name this cause directly — re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.

### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run

**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
backend restart/502 window.

**Pros (for).**
- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
  both runners.

**Cons (against).**
- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
  renewal/heartbeat path).
- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
  polls with no task impact.
- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
  better than the dominant offender.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
  proves this cause per case.
- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or
  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**
- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
  the 413 (Cause 2).
- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
  `finished`).

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix
  status.
- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.
- Post-rollout check: deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED
  completions with `gitFailure` payloads (per `1cae113f`), never as interrupts.

### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks

**Summary.** The reporter's alternate hypothesis, and what the UI label
("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts
(`deploy.sh` `restart_service`, crashes, OOM, operator restarts) orphan
`running_*` tasks, which reconcile to `interrupted` at boot.

**Pros (for).**
- Mechanically real: `deploy.sh` full deploys call `restart_service`
  (`systemctl --user restart kainbain.service`); the reconcile path exists and
  is tested (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`).
- A real backend restart/downtime window was observed 11-20 20:40:14–20:40:57
  (build 637 `deployedAt`, engine `updatedAt`, runner-visible 502s).
- The UI labels every auto-resume "after server restart", priming this reading.

**Cons (against — strong).**
- **Zero occurrences in retained history across all 61 tasks**: no `Stage
  execution interrupted by server restart`, no `Execution recovered after
  server restart`. All 118 interrupts are runner-initiated lease drops.
- The five most recent deploys (11-19 → 11-21, spanning the interruption spike)
  are all `--publish-only` (`registry + dist`), which `exit 0` before
  `restart_service` (`deploy.sh:1699-1712`, "prod untouched") — no restarts.
- The one observed restart (11-20 20:40) demonstrably orphaned nothing: the
  in-flight stage completed normally at 20:44:48.
- 1193 deploys in history with a 0-observed orphan rate suggests restarts
  either land on idle engines or claims survive them; either way this is not
  the current driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted (to keep this ruled out, cheaply).**
- Backend uptime/restarts: backend host journal for the API unit + `build.json`
  `deployedAt` vs `GET /status/observability` `engine.updatedAt` divergence as
  a restart detector.
- Ongoing: any future `interrupted by server restart` history line re-opens
  this cause immediately (grep task histories; currently zero).

## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake

These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:

- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
  or the operator to intervene.
- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
  into one scary number.
- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.

## 5. Evidence-wanted matrix (consolidated)

| # | Evidence | Source / command | Decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | local-alpha daemon journal 11-19 → 11-21 (`Runner failed:` lines + restart counters) | backend host `192.168.1.206`, `~server`, `journalctl --user -u <runner-unit>` | Cause 3 root fault; crash-loop vs re-claim loop |
| E2 | Backend access log 11-20 21:15–21:47 (five 413s, sizes) | backend host API/proxy logs | Cause 2 size-vs-limit confirmation |
| E3 | `Backend 413` journal sweep, both hosts, all dates | runner journals | Cause 2 scope beyond `7f6220c3` |
| E4 | Timestamp-join 502/`fetch failed` crashes vs server2-alpha interrupts | this host journal (have) + task histories (have) | Cause 4 per-case proof |
| E5 | Stage-output-commit presence per post-`finished` interrupt | `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3` preserved) | Cause 5 vs Cause 2/4 split |
| E6 | local-alpha build provenance + post-0.2.x bare-interrupt recount | fleet versions; re-run §2 counts after rollout | whether rollout resolves the bare 69 |
| E7 | Backend/proxy availability log 11-19 → 11-21 | backend host | Cause 4 window enumeration; Cause 6 upkeep |

Preservation notes: do not reap `kb-7f6220c3` (2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit with
pushed stage-output commits); retain journals quoted above (restart counters
830–834 at 11-20 21:47, 366–367 at 11-19 11:15).

## 6. Method note (reproducibility)

- Backend API (`http://192.168.1.206:3100`): `GET /tasks?projectId=0fd41821…`
  (61 tasks), full `GET /tasks/<id>` for each, `GET /status/observability`,
  `GET /deploy/status`, `GET /runners`; history actions pattern-counted
  (`interrupted execution`, `Auto-resumed after server restart`, `interrupted
  by server restart`, `Execution recovered after server restart`, `Runner
  deaths escalated`) and `started` → interrupt deltas computed from ISO
  timestamps.
- Repo: `api/flow/{startupRecovery,scheduler/*,executionLedger.js}`,
  `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`, `runner/{daemon.js,client.js,project.js}`,
  `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js`, `deploy.sh`,
  `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, `docs/tasks/1cae113f/SURVEY.md`.
- Runner host (this machine): `kb-7f6220c3` worktree git forensics; deployed
  runner `0.1.0` (`/home/server2/apps/kainbain/runner`, commit `f430f53`,
  no `interruptReason`); `journalctl --user -u
  kainbain-runner-server2-alpha` failure census since 11-19 (522 `Runner
  failed`: 501 `fetch failed`, 16 `Backend 502`, 5 `Backend 413`).
- Limits: local-alpha host (backend box) was not directly accessible — E1/E2/E7
  still open; task-history retention/capping was not verified, so very old
  interrupts could be undercounted; only project `0fd41821` was surveyed.

## 7. Cause scorecard

| Cause | Share it can explain | Confidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Worktree-cap loop | 49/118 (proven by reason strings) | high | confirmed contributor |
| 2. HTTP 413 on complete | 5 proven; ≤15 suspected | high (proven case) | confirmed, scope open (E3) |
| 3. local-alpha setup-phase deaths | up to ~60 bare/fast | medium (localised, fault unnamed) | needs E1 |
| 4. Backend-unreachable crashes mid-run | scattered bare | medium-low | needs E4/E7 |
| 5. Commit/push crash loop | 0 proven here; precedent `1cae113f` | medium (mechanism real, ruled out on examined case) | needs E5 |
| 6. Backend restarts orphaning tasks | 0/118 | high (ruled out as driver) | monitor only |
| Amplifier (§4) | multiplies all above | high | confirmed mechanics |

# Tickets created — interruption follow-ups for 2e663986

`GUIDE-01`–`GUIDE-07`, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`
(questions q1–q9, unanswered at creation time — each ticket cites its
survey question so the implementing agent can check for answers).

Target: project `0fd41821` (kainbain) / workflow `wf-default` / stage `1` (Idea).
API base used: `http://192.168.1.206:3100` (`localhost:3100` refused
connection from this runner; 192.168.1.206 is the backend host per the
runner env). All tickets created with `execute:false`, deterministic
`idempotencyKey = sha256(tag|1|<srcTask>)[0:32]`.

Dedupe: listed 71 tasks in wf-default; no open ticket duplicates S1–S7.
Two adjacent open tickets noted, not duplicated (referenced in goals):
`e3d4e9db` (runner-side setup-failure backoff — S1 is the backend-side
counterpart) and `fd5a74bf` (restart-storm detection observability).
Recursion guard: current task runs in `wf-bug-analysis-599cdd`,
stage `stage-1794587427152` — target stage `1` in `wf-default` is distinct.

## Created (8 of max 10)

| Tag | Ticket id | Title |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | `3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7` | Stop counting worktree-cap refusals as runner deaths; add re-dispatch backoff |
| S2 | `d164fb3f-ed08-4221-814e-e9e3a5d75a1a` | Fix the 413 completion-payload loop: raise limit, shrink payload, never crash on 413 |
| S6 | `79c51992-ab52-4f97-b35e-5a2aa605505d` | Fix misleading resume label and Tried-N-times inflation in task UI |
| S7 | `05b5d046-9480-40e3-8ec9-c06596c51acc` | Regression-pin boot reconcile so server-restart orphans stay at zero |
| S3 | `d9a9869c-46d3-4a57-9a69-a1a1ef87f9f8` | Investigate local-alpha setup-phase deaths via prod journal (evidence first) |
| S5 | `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` | Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount |
| S4 | `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e` | Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner |
| S3b | `810acb8f-9e6d-4ee0-8d80-4dddf8b1693b` | Fix the named local-alpha setup-phase fault found by the journal investigation |

Verified via `GET /tasks/<id>`: all have `currentStageId: "1"`,
status `waiting_human` (stage 1 is a human stage).

## Blocking

- `810acb8f` (S3b) has `blockedBy: ["d9a9869c-…"]` (S3) — verified on re-read.
  This is the only true code dependency per RESPONSE.md ("S3b is the only
  task blocked on another task's output").
- Deliberately NOT encoded as blocks: S5 "enables" prod confirmation of
  S2/S3/S4, but code work proceeds in parallel (per RESPONSE.md §Blocking
  map), so blocking would wrongly serialize them — recorded as coordination
  notes in the goals instead. S4's sequencing with `db49d6c6` needs no
  block (that task is completed) — recorded as a must-read in the goal.

Each ticket goal's first line is its one-line title, and includes an
evidence snippet from RESPONSE.md plus file/test references for the
implementing agent.
