### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)

**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).

**Pros (for).**
- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
  11-20 (18).
- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
  (only uncaught fallible step there).
- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.

**Cons (against).**
- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
  restart counters are unknown from here.
- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`
  (12× local) — need the **local-alpha daemon journal on the backend host**
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`, systemd user unit) for those windows: the
  `Runner failed: <message>` line names the fault, and restart-counter lines
  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.
- local-alpha build provenance: confirm it is also pre-11-21 (expected bare);
  after the 0.2.x rollout, bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should
  name this cause directly — re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.

### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run

**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
backend restart/502 window.

**Pros (for).**
- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
  both runners.

**Cons (against).**
- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
  renewal/heartbeat path).
- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
  polls with no task impact.
- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
  better than the dominant offender.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
  proves this cause per case.
- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or
  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**
- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
  the 413 (Cause 2).
- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
  `finished`).

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix
  status.
- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.
- Post-rollout check: deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED
  completions with `gitFailure` payloads (per `1cae113f`), never as interrupts.

### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks

**Summary.** The reporter's alternate hypothesis, and what the UI label
("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts
(`deploy.sh` `restart_service`, crashes, OOM, operator restarts) orphan
`running_*` tasks, which reconcile to `interrupted` at boot.

**Pros (for).**
- Mechanically real: `deploy.sh` full deploys call `restart_service`
  (`systemctl --user restart kainbain.service`); the reconcile path exists and
  is tested (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`).
- A real backend restart/downtime window was observed 11-20 20:40:14–20:40:57
  (build 637 `deployedAt`, engine `updatedAt`, runner-visible 502s).
- The UI labels every auto-resume "after server restart", priming this reading.

**Cons (against — strong).**
- **Zero occurrences in retained history across all 61 tasks**: no `Stage
  execution interrupted by server restart`, no `Execution recovered after
  server restart`. All 118 interrupts are runner-initiated lease drops.
- The five most recent deploys (11-19 → 11-21, spanning the interruption spike)
  are all `--publish-only` (`registry + dist`), which `exit 0` before
  `restart_service` (`deploy.sh:1699-1712`, "prod untouched") — no restarts.
- The one observed restart (11-20 20:40) demonstrably orphaned nothing: the
  in-flight stage completed normally at 20:44:48.
- 1193 deploys in history with a 0-observed orphan rate suggests restarts
  either land on idle engines or claims survive them; either way this is not
  the current driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted (to keep this ruled out, cheaply).**
- Backend uptime/restarts: backend host journal for the API unit + `build.json`
  `deployedAt` vs `GET /status/observability` `engine.updatedAt` divergence as
  a restart detector.
- Ongoing: any future `interrupted by server restart` history line re-opens
  this cause immediately (grep task histories; currently zero).

## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake

These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:

- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
  or the operator to intervene.
- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
  into one scary number.
- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report."}

+  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
+  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
+  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
+  rollout.
+- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
+  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
+  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
+- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
+  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
+  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
+- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
+  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.
+
+**Cons (against).**
+- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
+  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
+  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
+  the 413 (Cause 2).
+- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
+  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
+  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
+  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
+- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
+  `finished`).
+
+**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
+- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
+  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix
+  status.
+- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
+  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
+  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.
+- Post-rollout check: deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED
+  completions with `gitFailure` payloads (per `1cae113f`), never as interrupts.
+
+### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks
+
+**Summary.** The reporter's alternate hypothesis, and what the UI label
+("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts
+(`deploy.sh` `restart_service`, crashes, OOM, operator restarts) orphan
+`running_*` tasks, which reconcile to `interrupted` at boot.
+
+**Pros (for).**
+- Mechanically real: `deploy.sh` full deploys call `restart_service`
+  (`systemctl --user restart kainbain.service`); the reconcile path exists and
+  is tested (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`).
+- A real backend restart/downtime window was observed 11-20 20:40:14–20:40:57
+  (build 637 `deployedAt`, engine `updatedAt`, runner-visible 502s).
+- The UI labels every auto-resume "after server restart", priming this reading.
+
+**Cons (against — strong).**
+- **Zero occurrences in retained history across all 61 tasks**: no `Stage
+  execution interrupted by server restart`, no `Execution recovered after
+  server restart`. All 118 interrupts are runner-initiated lease drops.
+- The five most recent deploys (11-19 → 11-21, spanning the interruption spike)
+  are all `--publish-only` (`registry + dist`), which `exit 0` before
+  `restart_service` (`deploy.sh:1699-1712`, "prod untouched") — no restarts.
+- The one observed restart (11-20 20:40) demonstrably orphaned nothing: the
+  in-flight stage completed normally at 20:44:48.
+- 1193 deploys in history with a 0-observed orphan rate suggests restarts
+  either land on idle engines or claims survive them; either way this is not
+  the current driver.
+
+**Tasks / evidence wanted (to keep this ruled out, cheaply).**
+- Backend uptime/restarts: backend host journal for the API unit + `build.json`
+  `deployedAt` vs `GET /status/observability` `engine.updatedAt` divergence as
+  a restart detector.
+- Ongoing: any future `interrupted by server restart` history line re-opens
+  this cause immediately (grep task histories; currently zero).
+
+## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake
+
+These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
+"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:
+
+- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
+  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
+  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
+  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
+  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
+  or the operator to intervene.
+- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
+  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
+  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
+  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
+  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
+  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
+- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
+  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
+  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
+  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
+  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
+  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
+  into one scary number.
+- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
+  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
+  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
+  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.

# AGENTS-MAP — one-page orientation (read after `agents.md`, before any `ls`/`find`)

**Orientation in ≤3 reads:** 1) `agents.md` → 2) this file → 3) the one entry
file your change touches (grep for a symbol listed below — never read a god file whole).

## Directory ownership and reviewer roles

Roster sourced from `docs/ARCHITECTURE_DOMAINS.md`; role titles only, never individual
names. A PR touching a row needs the matching reviewer; cross-domain changes need every
affected reviewer. Until a volunteer steps up, the domain reviewer for the most-affected
area stands in as **Docs Steward**.

| Dir | Owns | Owner role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api/work/` | Task identity, assets, branches, errors, files, lifecycle, finalize, persistence, survey, workspace, task-work routes | Work reviewer |
| `api/flow/` | Scheduler, execution queue, stage execution/advancement/failback, flow routes, command stages, reports gating (`execution/`, `routing/{tables,resolvers,orchestrators}/`, `scheduler/`) | Flow reviewer |
| `api/watch/` | Observability: process logs, log-feed routes, stage reports, metrics, reliability | Watch reviewer |
| `api/house/` | Project startup, safe atomic file writing | House reviewer |
| `api/auth/` | (Access domain) Organisation sign-in (OIDC), sessions, users, roles, guards, auth routes | House reviewer |
| `api/crew/` | Harness roster, model discovery, session capabilities | Crew reviewer |
| `api/agent/` | Harness boundary (pi, antigravity, muse, vibe, opencode, custom, mock), contracts, `logStream/` | Crew reviewer |
| `api/git/` | (WP-4) Command-family git operations: errors, validation, exec, staleLock, status, working-tree status/recovery, branch, commit, merge, remote — each under 420 LOC, covered by co-located `*.test.js` | Work reviewer |
| `api/project/` | (WP-3) Project normalizers/utilities: `stageNormalizers`, `retrySettings`, `appStatus`, `workflowDefaults`, `aliasRenames`, `deployCommands`, `projectSlug`, `gitRemote`, `projectConfigDiscovery` — each under 400 LOC; consumed only through `api/projectStore.js` | House reviewer |
| `api/routes/` | Fastify route registrars (thin); `tasks.js` is a 45-line facade → work/flow/watch route modules | House reviewer |
| `api/skills/` | Skills registry and stage skill injection | Flow reviewer |
| `api/index.js` | Fastify server wiring only; registration, no business logic (resolvers in `api/projectResolution.js`, `api/sessionResolution.js`, CORS in `api/cors.js`) | House reviewer |
| `frontend/src/components/workflow/` | Workflow canvas and extracted hooks | Flow reviewer |
| `frontend/src/components/workflow/hooks/` | Extracted canvas state logic: `useActivityConsole`, `useBoardFilters`, `useCanvasAnalytics`, `useCanvasSearchFilter`, `useCollapsedGroups`, `useMobileToolbarCollapse`, `useStageDnD`, `useStageTagFilter`, `useTaskActions` | Flow reviewer |
| `frontend/src/components/tasks/` | Task identity, overlay/tab panes, work actions, reports/logs/history panes | Work reviewer |
| `frontend/src/components/settings/` | Project settings, system settings, house config UI | House reviewer |
| `frontend/src/context/` | App context composed from domain hooks (no split; see §No-split decisions) | House reviewer |
| `frontend/src/services/` | API client facade over work/flow/crew/watch/house domains | domain owners |
| `shared/` | Shared api↔frontend constants and helpers (`toolLogFormat`, report helpers, model keys/aliases, stage keyword tokens) | Watch reviewer for `toolLogFormat`; Crew reviewer for model keys/aliases; Flow reviewer for stage keyword tokens |
| `site-docs/` | Markdown docs served by `GET /docs` | Docs Steward + affected domain reviewer |
| `tests/`, `scripts/` | Bash/Node test harnesses, utility scripts | Docs Steward for doc-facing scripts; Platform owner for the rest |
| `docs/` | Curated architecture/plan/guide notes (tracked) | Docs Steward |
| _(notes space, out-of-repo)_ | Frozen run archive: per-task engine artifacts and historical decision records | Docs Steward (rotation) — see `docs/TASK_DIRECTORY_HYGIENE.md` |

## No-split decisions

- `frontend/src/context/KainBainContext.jsx` (~470 LOC) intentionally stays a single shell composed from focused `use*` hooks in `frontend/src/context/`. No split PR is pending; do not expect one. Satellite hooks: `useBoardSync.js`, `useAccentTheme.js`, `useSelectedTask`, `useViewNavigation` (among others).
- `frontend/src/services/api.js` is a compatibility facade; new requests go in `frontend/src/services/{work,flow,crew,watch,house}/index.js`.
- `api/taskStore.js` and `api/projectStore.js` remain class + singleton facades; pure logic lives in `api/work/` and `api/project/`.

## Barrels that look like code but aren't

- `api/projectStore.js` (~2254 LOC): `ProjectStore` class + singleton wiring only; pure normalizers/utilities live in `api/project/` (WP-3). Registry wiring and persistence stay in the barrel.
- `api/taskStore.js` (~1069 LOC): `TaskStore` class + singleton wiring over `api/{work,flow,watch,house}/index.js` — every method delegates to those subdirs, no business logic lives here. Engine-state composition, owner snapshot, open-queue depth, cwd/link seams, wedge settlement, scheduler kick, and never-throw push seams live as single-purpose modules in `api/work/`. `api/work/index.js` re-exports every cycle-free work module (route registrars stay out — `taskWorkRoutes.js` imports `api/flow/`).

import { _appendLogEntries, _appendProcessLog } from "../watch/index.js";
import { config } from "../config.js";
import { git } from "../git.js";
import { createLogProcessor } from "../agent/logStream/logProcessor.js";
import { attachAttestationToEntry } from "../../shared/stageAttestation.js";

/***
 * MARK: MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS
 * @description Bound on consecutive Runner-death interrupts for one
 *   task+stage (G7): a Runner that keeps dying mid-stage re-queues as
 *   `interrupted` each time, but past this many in a row the interrupt
 *   escalates (history entry + `interruptEscalations` monitor counter +
 *   `escalated` reply flag) so the death loop gets operator attention
 *   instead of spinning forever. A successful completion resets the count.
 * @example MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS => 5
 ***/
export const MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5;
export { formatPosture, servingModelFor } from "./runnerPosture.js";
import { cleanReportedPosture } from "./runnerPosture.js";

/***
 * MARK: ExecutionLedger
 * @description Backend receiving side of the Runner wire protocol (ADR 0009
 *   lifecycle steps 4–6): sequenced progress events, sequenced log frames,
 *   idempotent completion, and interruption. Every mutating call first
 *   checks the ClaimStore lease — a stale epoch is rejected before any
 *   state changes, which is what makes a partitioned zombie's late report
 *   a 409 instead of a double completion (R01). Dedupe is per execution:
 *   a retried report is a recorded no-op, never a duplicate stage (step 4).
 *   Log gaps are represented in the data ("frames missing — Runner
 *   disconnected"), never papered over (R14). Completion records the
 *   Runner's report (SHA/branch/posture) and releases the lease; stage
 *   advancement stays engine-owned until the dispatch integration lands.
 *   WP1 tenant fence (AUDIT H-4): the lease also names its home project
 *   (`hold.projectId`), and every guarded write must name the same one —
 *   a mismatch throws 409 PROJECT_FENCE_MISMATCH, counts
 *   `fencedRejected`, audits on the lease's home task, and leaves the
 *   original hold untouched. Consecutive Runner-death interrupts escalate
 *   past MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS (G7). Monitor counters back the Phase 2
 *   "pageable-zero" reconcile/divergence signals. In-memory for Phase 2
 *   (same durability story as ClaimStore).
 * @example const ledger = new ExecutionLedger()
 * @example ledger.snapshot() => { progressRecorded: 0, … }
 ***/
export class ExecutionLedger {
	constructor() {
		this.seenProgress = new Set();
		this.logNextSeq = new Map();
		this.logEventNextSeq = new Map();
		this.logProcessors = new Map();
		this.lastStage = new Map();
		this.stagePrompt = new Map();
		this.stageServing = new Map();
		this.counters = {
			progressRecorded: 0,
			progressDuplicates: 0,
			logFrames: 0,
			logGaps: 0,
			logDuplicates: 0,
			logEventBatches: 0,
			logEventGaps: 0,
			logEventDuplicates: 0,
			logEventsDropped: 0,
			completions: 0,
			completionDuplicates: 0,
			staleRejected: 0,
			fencedRejected: 0,
			interrupts: 0,
			interruptEscalations: 0,
			divergences: 0,
			unverifiedSha: 0,

#!/usr/bin/env node
/***
 * MARK: run-tests.mjs
 * @description Cross-platform full-project verification gate: the same seven
 *   checks the old `run-tests.sh` ran plus the Container Tests branch, the
 *   Frontend Build branch (exercises the deprecation gate), the Dependency
 *   Audit Gate, the Proof Hygiene branch, and the Binary Guard branch, in a
 *   single overlap window
 *   (the two unit suites
 *   alone take ~2x35s sequentially, so overlapping keeps the wall near one
 *   suite), with identical `Running <name>... PASS/FAIL (<s>s)` lines and exit semantics —
 *   but driven by Node (`node:child_process`, no shell), so it runs on
 *   Linux, macOS, and Windows with only Node + npm installed. Shells out
 *   only to `npm`/Node/Docker; the two environment-conditional branches
 *   report SKIP instead of failing when their runtime is absent (Security
 *   Script Tests without `bash`, Container Tests without a Docker daemon).
 *   The fast branches share one overlap window; the Canary Tests branch runs
 *   alone afterwards (see splitGatePhases) — same suites, same exit
 *   semantics, but the heaviest branch never shares CPUs with the unit
 *   suites. Fail-fast is ON by default (see resolveFailFast): when the fast
 *   phase fails, the gate writes its verdict (`verdict.json` plus one
 *   untrimmed `<branch-slug>.full.log` per failed branch) under
 *   `$KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS/ci-fast-gate-<timestamp>/`, prints the
 *   `KAINBAIN_FAST_GATE_RESULT` banner, and skips the serial canary phase
 *   with an explicit SKIP line — so the failure surfaces seconds after the
 *   fast phase instead of ~13 minutes later. Opt out with `--no-fail-fast`
 *   or `KAINBAIN_NO_FAIL_FAST=1` (canary still runs after a red fast phase,
 *   but the verdict still lands early). A green fast phase always runs
 *   canary (the #KB-0417 parity requirement); deploy.sh --prod passes
 *   `--no-canary` to its final-test-suite gate, so fail-fast changes
 *   nothing there. Failure Details tails stay bounded (120 lines by
 *   default, `KAINBAIN_FAILURE_TAIL_LINES` to tune) with a `Full log:`
 *   pointer at the untrimmed file; the verdict pointers are printed at the
 *   gate's head and tail so they survive the engine's head+tail excerpts.
 *   The Container Tests branch runs the static Dockerfile/compose assertions
 *   only; the minutes-long live image build/boot tests are opt-in via
 *   `KAINBAIN_CONTAINER_TESTS=live` (direct suite run, not the gate).
 *   The Canary Tests branch (serial Playwright suite on its own scratch
 *   stack, ~7 min) is IN the default gate so `npm test` and
 *   `deploy.sh --prod` run the exact same suites and regressions surface in
 *   the earliest automated stage, not at the merge/deploy gate (the
 *   #KB-0417 incident). Opt out with `--no-canary` or
 *   `KAINBAIN_SKIP_CANARY=1` for fast sanity cycles; `deploy.sh --prod`
 *   passes `--no-canary` to its `final-test-suite` gate and runs the canary
 *   suite as its own blocking `canary-e2e` gate, so nothing runs twice.
 *   Measured gate wall is ~60-70s without canary (the two unit suites alone
 *   are ~160s of CPU work) and ~366-420s with canary (the serial Playwright
 *   suite is minutes long), so CI stages running this gate need an explicit
 *   `timeout` override well above the 60s engine default
 *   (`config.ciTimeoutMs`) — this project's stage sets 1800s. While branches
 *   run the gate emits `▸ started <name>` lines and a `⏳ still running: …`
 *   tick every 30s (`KAINBAIN_GATE_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS`), so a slow branch
 *   never blanks the output (see scripts/lib/run-parallel.mjs).
 *   `run-tests.sh` is a thin shim over this file so `deploy.sh --prod` and
 *   older docs keep working.
 * @example `npm test` => thirteen PASS lines (twelve fast branches + Canary Tests), exit 0
 * @example `npm test -- --no-canary` => twelve PASS lines, exit 0
 ***/

1|# TDD Test Examples — consolidated recipes for the interruption flakes
2|
3|All snippets are for a follow-up **code stage** (this stage is docs-only, so
4|no test files were added to the repo). Each recipe: red test first (it should
5|fail or pin current behaviour), then the code change that turns it green.
6|Full snippets live in the per-cause guides linked below; this file is the
7|map + run commands.
8|
9|## Where each test would live and how to run it
10|
11|| Guide | Proposed test file | Runner | Command |
12||---|---|---|---|
13|| GUIDE-01 cap loop | `runner/project.worktreeCap.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/project.worktreeCap.test.js` |
14|| GUIDE-01 backend | `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` |
15|| GUIDE-02 413 | `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js`, `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js bodyLimit.default.test.js` |
16|| GUIDE-02 payload | `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` |
17|| GUIDE-03 storm | `api/flow/scheduler/bareInterruptStorm.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/bareInterruptStorm.test.js` |
18|| GUIDE-03 setup faults | `runner/project.setupFaults.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/project.setupFaults.test.js` |
19|| GUIDE-04 outage | `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` |
20|| GUIDE-05 hook loop | `runner/gitOps.hookCrashLoop.test.js` | node:test | `node --test runner/gitOps.hookCrashLoop.test.js` |
21|| GUIDE-05 backend | `api/flow/executionLedger.commitLoop.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/executionLedger.commitLoop.test.js` |
22|| GUIDE-06 reconcile | `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` |
23|| GUIDE-07 label | `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` |
24|| GUIDE-07 priority | `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` | vitest | `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` |
25|| GUIDE-07 tryCount | additions to `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js` | vitest | `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js` |
26|
27|Housekeeping for the code stage:
28|
29|- New `runner/*.test.js` files MUST be added to the explicit list in
30|  `scripts/run-tests.mjs` `buildBranches()` ("Unit Tests (runner)") —
31|  `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins that every runner suite is registered.
32|- New/renamed exports in `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/` need a JSDoc
33|  block with `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example`; run
34|  `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1 s) before pushing.
35|- Full gate: `npm test` (or `npm test -- --no-canary` for a fast cycle);
36|  per-area: `npm run test:api`, `npm run test:frontend`.
37|
38|## TDD workflow per issue
39|
40|1. **Write the red test** from the guide (most are written to FAIL against
41|   current code — they encode the desired fix: cap refusals not counted as
42|   deaths, distinct resume label, Resumed rows excluded from tryCount,
43|   non-fatal transient backend errors, backoff on repeated resumes).
44|2. **Run it, confirm red.**
45|3. **Change the seam** named in the guide (`executionLedger.js`,
46|   `autoResumeTask.js`, `taskFormatters.js`, `daemon.js` catch, …).
47|4. **Run green**, then the full gate.
48|5. Tests that only PIN current behaviour (marked "PIN" in the guides, e.g.
49|   the 413 default, the reconcile flip) should pass immediately — they are
50|   regression guards, not red tests.
51|
52|## What CANNOT be tested locally — do not attempt without explicit user permission
53|
54|| Item | Why | Tier | Where documented |
55||---|---|---|---|
56|| Root cause of local-alpha bare setup deaths | Deployed 0.1.0 attaches no reason; only the local-alpha host journal (192.168.1.206) names it | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-03 §4 (E1) |
57|| Fleet-wide interrupt recount / before-after 0.2.x rollout | Live backend API, project `0fd41821` | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-03 §4 (E6), GUIDE-07 §5 |
58|| 413 confirmation on real tasks (`7f6220c3`) + journal sweeps | Runner journals + backend access log on prod hosts | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-02 §4 (E2/E3) |
59|| Crash-vs-reclaim join for server2-alpha interrupts | server2 journal + task histories | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-04 §4 (E4) |
60|| Backend downtime window enumeration | backend/proxy logs on prod host | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-04 §4 (E7) |
61|| Worktree forensics on `kb-<taskId>` exhibits | Runner hosts; do NOT reap `kb-7f6220c3` | PROD-READ-ONLY | GUIDE-02 §4, GUIDE-05 §4 (E5) |
62|| Any re-run of a real agent stage (e.g. resuming parked `7f6220c3`) | Invokes a real agent against the live backend, burns a stage run, mutates task state | PROD-ACTION | GUIDE-03 §4 |
63|| Restarting/reaping prod runners or backend to force a repro | Mutates shared prod systems | PROD-ACTION | — (not recommended; observe only) |
64|
65|None of the PROD-READ-ONLY / PROD-ACTION commands in the guides were
66|executed for this stage. They are procedures only — **run them only with
67|explicit user permission**.
68|
69|## Safe local e2e option (no prod, still opt-in)
70|
71|A full loop reproduction without touching prod is possible against a
72|**scratch stack**: `docker compose up` a dev backend on localhost, register a
73|local runner, create a scratch project, pre-fill the runner work root with 5
74|fresh `kb-*` dirs (Cause 1) or install a failing pre-commit hook in the
75|scratch project (Cause 5), then watch `GET /tasks/<id>` history. This still
76|invokes a real agent harness, so treat it as opt-in and time-boxed; the unit
77|recipes above cover the same mechanics without an agent.

6|## 0. Inputs

21|## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)
22|
23|Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):
24|
25|1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
26|   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
27|   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
28|   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
29|   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
30|   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
31|2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
32|   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
33|   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
34|   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
35|   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
36|   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
37|   an authenticated runner daemon.
38|
39|Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
40|`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
41|`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
42|server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
43|function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
44|`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
45|same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
46|(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
47|(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).
48|
49|## 2. Fleet-wide numbers (live backend, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21)
50|
51|| Signal | Count | Notes |
52||---|---|---|
53|| Runner-path interrupts (`interrupted execution`) | 118 | across 30/61 tasks (~half the project) |
54|| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
55|| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
56|| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
57|| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
58|| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
59|| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
60|| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
61|| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
62|| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |
63|
64|Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
65|(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
66|`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
67|try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
68|localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
69|Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
70|`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.
71|
72|Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
73|`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
74|worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
75|and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
76|`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle
77|converge (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so rollout lag is expected.
78|
79|## 3. Possible causes
80|
81|### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)
82|
83|**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
84|workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
85|reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
86|Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full

88|the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a

101|- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
102|  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
103|  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

106|- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap

110|- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
111|- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike

123|### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)
124|
125|**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
126|(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
127|backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
128|(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
129|a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
130|agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
131|each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
132|run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
133|(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
134|up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
135|top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
136|output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
137|(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`; the only explicit `bodyLimit` in the
138|API is the accessibility route).
139|
140|**Pros (for).**
141|- Smoking gun in the server2-alpha journal (`journalctl --user
142|  -u kainbain-runner-server2-alpha`): on 11-20, five consecutive cycles of
143|  `Committed <sha> (pushed: true)` → `Runner failed: Backend 413 on
144|  /tasks/7f6220c3-.../complete-execution` → `Main process exited, status=1`
145|  → `Scheduled restart job, restart counter 830→834`, at 21:19, 21:29, 21:35,
146|  21:43, 21:47 — exactly matching the five `finished` → bare-interrupt pairs
147|  in task `7f6220c3` history.
148|- Worktree forensics agree: `kb-7f6220c3` holds the pushed stage-output commits
149|  with matching timestamps, and `origin` has them — proving failure happened
150|  strictly after push.
151|- Deterministic: same task files every lap → same 413 → loop only ends via the
152|  death-bound park (observed: parked at count 7).
153|- Explains why the newest, longest, most asset-heavy stages (Merge resolver
154|  with proof screenshots) interrupt while short stages complete.
155|
156|**Cons (against).**
157|- Proven for exactly one task-stage so far (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 5
158|  interrupts); the other 10 post-`finished` bare interrupts are unexamined.
159|- Cannot explain the 99 sub-15s interrupts (413 only happens at completion,
160|  minutes in).
161|- Backend 413 leaves no task-history trace of its own (the backend rejects
162|  before routing), so backend history alone can never confirm/deny further
163|  cases — runner journals are required.
164|
165|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
166|- `7f6220c3` (screenshot task; Merge-resolver window 11-20 21:15–21:47):
167|  backend access/error log for the five 413s (confirm size vs limit);
168|  preserve `kb-7f6220c3` worktree (do not reap) — 2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit.
169|- Journal sweep on both runner hosts for `Backend 413` across all tasks/dates
170|  (server2-alpha: 5 hits since 11-19, all this task; local-alpha journal still
171|  needed — host `192.168.1.206`, user `server`).
172|- Any other task whose `finished` → interrupt gap is seconds with a preceding
173|  multi-minute run is a 413 suspect; check runner journals first, backend
174|  history second (it will be bare).

176|### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)
177|
178|**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
179|(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
180|`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
181|residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
182|re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
183|matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
184|is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
185|generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).
186|
187|**Pros (for).**
188|- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
189|  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
190|  11-20 (18).
191|- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
192|  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
193|  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
194|  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
195|- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
196|  (only uncaught fallible step there).
197|- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
198|  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.
199|
200|**Cons (against).**
201|- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
202|  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
203|  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
204|  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
205|- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
206|  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
207|  restart counters are unknown from here.
208|- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
209|  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.

212|- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20

223|### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run
224|
225|**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
226|failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
227|systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
228|progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
229|interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
230|remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
231|backend restart/502 window.
232|
233|**Pros (for).**
234|- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
235|  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
236|  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
237|  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
238|- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
239|  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
240|  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
241|  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
242|- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
243|  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
244|  both runners.
245|
246|**Cons (against).**
247|- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
248|  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
249|  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
250|  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
251|  renewal/heartbeat path).
252|- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
253|  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
254|  polls with no task impact.
255|- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
256|  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
257|  better than the dominant offender.
258|
259|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
260|- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
261|  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
262|  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
263|  proves this cause per case.
264|- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or

266|- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
267|  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
268|  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

270|### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)
271|
272|**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
273|generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
274|re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
275|(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
276|death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
277|class.
278|
279|**Pros (for).**
280|- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
281|  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
282|  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
283|  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
284|  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
285|  rollout.
286|- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
287|  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
288|  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
289|- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
290|  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
291|  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
292|- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
293|  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.
294|
295|**Cons (against).**
296|- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
297|  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
298|  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
299|  the 413 (Cause 2).
300|- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
301|  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
302|  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
303|  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
304|- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
305|  `finished`).
306|
307|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
308|- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
309|  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix

311|- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`

317|### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks

320|("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts

352|## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake
353|
354|These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
355|"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:
356|
357|- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
358|  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
359|  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
360|  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
361|  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
362|  or the operator to intervene.
363|- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
364|  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
365|  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
366|  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
367|  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
368|  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
369|- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
370|  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
371|  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
372|  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
373|  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
374|  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
375|  into one scary number.
376|- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
377|  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
378|  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
379|  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.

8|all 118 observed interrupts were runner-initiated lease drops. The five most

11|real restart (11-20 20:40, build 637) orphaned nothing. Keep as monitor-only.

33|## 2. Safe local replication (api, vitest)

40|import { ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES } from "./orphanedRunningStatuses.js";

42|function mockStore(tasks) {
43|  const history = [];
44|  const store = {
45|    projectStore: { listProjects: () => [{ id: "p1", cwd: "/tmp/p1" }] },
46|    listTasks: () => tasks,
47|    engineState: { activeTaskId: "t-live" }, // the engine's own task is never reconciled
48|    _recordHistory: (task, action) => history.push({ task: task.id, action }),
49|    _saveTaskMarkdown: () => {},
50|  };
51|  return { store, history };
52|}
53|
54|test("orphaned running_* tasks flip to interrupted with the server-restart history row", () => {
55|  const tasks = [
56|    { id: "t-orphan", status: "running_agent", history: [] },
57|    { id: "t-live", status: "running_agent", history: [] },   // engine-owned: untouched
58|    { id: "t-adv", status: "advancing", history: [] },
59|    { id: "t-ok", status: "in_stage", history: [] },
60|  ];
61|  const { store, history } = mockStore(tasks);
62|  const out = reconcileInterruptedRuns(store);
63|  expect(out).toEqual([{ projectId: "p1", taskId: "t-orphan" }, { projectId: "p1", taskId: "t-adv" }]);

65|  expect(tasks[0].wasInterrupted).toBe(true);

68|    "Stage execution interrupted by server restart",
69|    "Stage execution interrupted by server restart",
70|  ]);
71|});
72|

75|  const { store } = mockStore(tasks);
76|  expect(reconcileInterruptedRuns(store)).toHaveLength(1);
77|  expect(reconcileInterruptedRuns(store)).toEqual([]);
78|});
79|

98|## 3. Safe local replication — why task files can trigger it (runner, `node:test`)
99|
100|`collectTaskFiles` caps the *files array* at 1 MiB cumulative, but the JSON
101|envelope adds the (up to 20 KiB) `output`, attestation, posture and JSON
102|escaping — and binary assets read as utf8 can inflate. Pin the boundary.
103|Proposed file (code stage): `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js`
104|
105|```js
106|import { describe, it, afterEach } from "node:test";
107|import assert from "node:assert/strict";
108|import fs from "node:fs"; import os from "node:os"; import path from "node:path";
109|import { collectTaskFiles } from "./daemon.js";
110|
111|it("many sub-256KiB files are collectively capped near 1 MiB — envelope+output can still push the POST over the Fastify limit", () => {
112|  const workdir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "kb-files-"));
113|  const dir = path.join(workdir, "docs", "tasks", "t1");
114|  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
115|  // 6 x 200 KiB "PNGs" (each under the 256 KiB per-file cap) + task.md
116|  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, `shot${i}.png`), Buffer.alloc(200 * 1024, 1));
117|  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "task.md"), "ignore me");
118|  const files = collectTaskFiles({ workdir, taskId: "t1" });
119|  const total = files.reduce((n, f) => n + Buffer.byteLength(f.content, "utf8"), 0);
120|  assert.ok(total <= 1024 * 1024, "file payload itself stays under 1 MiB");
121|  assert.ok(files.some((f) => f.name === "shot5.png") === false, "files past the cumulative cap are skipped");
122|  // …so the 413 comes from files(≤1MiB) + output(20KiB) + JSON overhead > 1 MiB
123|  const body = JSON.stringify({ taskFiles: files, output: "o".repeat(20_000) });
124|  assert.ok(Buffer.byteLength(body) > 1024 * 1024, "full complete-execution body exceeds Fastify default");

1|# GUIDE 03 — local-alpha setup-phase deaths (bare interrupt ~5 s after `started`, no `prompted`)
2|
3|Cause 3 in `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` — the volume-dominant signature: 96/118
4|interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide land <=15 s after `started`
5|(median 4.7 s) with no `prompted` event, i.e. the run dies inside worktree
6|preparation. This is the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident.
7|
8|- **Verdict: PARTIAL locally.** The *backend side* of the loop (bare
9|  interrupt -> instant Rule-0 re-queue -> escalation park) is unit-testable
10|  with mocks, and `prepareWorkdir` failure shapes are reproducible in temp
11|  dirs. The **root fault on the local-alpha host is PROD-READ-ONLY** — the
12|  deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the generic path, so only the
13|  local-alpha daemon journal names it. A full end-to-end repro needs a real
14|  runner claiming a real task — PROD-ACTION unless run against a fully local
15|  scratch stack.
16|- **Code seams:** `runner/daemon.js:1975` (`started` progress) ->
17|  `:1984` (`prepareWorkdir`, the only uncaught fallible step) ->
18|  `:2061` (`prompted`); generic catch `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`
19|  (0.2.0 attaches `interruptReason`, still rethrows -> `exit(1)` -> systemd
20|  restart; deployed 0.1.0 predates `046a6391` so it is bare); backend:
21|  `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution`,
22|  `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`,
23|  `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.js` (Rule-0 pickup).
24|
25|## 1. Signature (recognise it)
26|
27|- Task history: **bare** interrupt (`…lease dropped, re-queues as
28|  interrupted` with NO `Reason:`) <=15 s after the runner's `started` event,
29|  no `prompted` in between; then `Auto-resumed after server restart —
30|  prioritised in queue`; repeat every ~18–60 s until `Runner deaths
31|  escalated` at 5 on the same stage.
32|- Exhibits: `c5c465c4` (28 bare local-alpha interrupts, 11-19 12:15–12:37,
33|  ~18 s apart); `7f6220c3` In-Progress loop 11-20 15:38–15:43 (x5), Quick
34|  review 18:39–18:41 (x4), single-shots 11-21 10:16 and 13:34.
35|- Runner journal (prod): either `Runner failed: <message>` + `restart
36|  counter` increments (true crash loop) or tight claim->interrupt->re-claim
37|  with no restart (in-process loop) — backend history cannot distinguish
38|  these two; only the journal can.
39|
40|## 2. Safe local replication — backend side of the loop (api, vitest)
41|
42|Simulate a runner that keeps dying in setup: repeated interrupts with
43|`reason: null` (what 0.1.0 sent), assert the bare history row, the Rule-0
44|resume label, and the park at the bound. Proposed file (code stage):
45|`api/flow/scheduler/bareInterruptStorm.test.js`
46|
47|```js
48|import { describe, test, expect } from "vitest";
49|import { ExecutionLedger, MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS } from "../executionLedger.js";
50|import { autoResumeTask } from "./autoResumeTask.js";
51|import { isAutoResumableWithReason } from "./isAutoResumableWithReason.js";
52|// mock store/claimStore as in api/flow/executionLedger.test.js
53|
54|test("bare setup-phase interrupts: reasonless history, instant auto-resume, park at the bound", () => {
55|  const ledger = new ExecutionLedger();
56|  let task = ctx.taskStore.getTask();
57|  for (let i = 1; i <= MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS; i++) {
58|    const { executionId } = claimed(ctx);
59|    ledger.interruptExecution({ claimStore: ctx.claimStore, taskStore: ctx.taskStore,
60|      projectId: "p1", taskId: "t1", runnerId: "local-alpha", executionId, reason: null });
61|    const h = task.history.at(-1).action;
62|    if (i < MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS) expect(h).toMatch(/lease dropped, re-queues as interrupted$/); // bare: no Reason
63|    autoResumeTask(ctx.store, "p1", "t1"); // scheduleTick pickup
64|    expect(task.status).toBe("in_stage");
65|    expect(task.history.at(-1).action).toBe("Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue");
66|  }
67|  const verdict = isAutoResumableWithReason(task, { type: "agent" });
68|  expect(verdict).toEqual({ resumable: false, reason: "runner-death-loop" });
69|});
70|```
71|
72|TDD angle: after the 0.2.x rollout lands on runners, bare interrupts should
73|vanish. Red-test the desired end state now: `interruptExecution(..., reason: null)`
74|from an old-version runner should still record *something* useful — e.g. assert
75|the history row contains the runner version, watch it fail, then implement.
76|
77|Run: `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/bareInterruptStorm.test.js`
78|
79|## 3. Safe local replication — `prepareWorkdir` failure shapes (runner, `node:test`)
80|
81|Reproduce "dies seconds after `started`, before `prompted`" by forcing each
82|fallible setup input to fail in a temp work root:
83|
84|Proposed file (code stage): `runner/project.setupFaults.test.js`
85|
86|```js
87|import { describe, it, beforeEach, afterEach } from "node:test";
88|import assert from "node:assert/strict";
89|import fs from "node:fs"; import os from "node:os"; import path from "node:path";
90|import { prepareWorkdir } from "./project.js";
91|
92|let workRoot, src;
93|beforeEach(() => {
94|  workRoot = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "kb-setup-"));
95|  src = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "kb-setup-src-"));
96|  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(src, "f.txt"), "x");
97|});
98|afterEach(() => { fs.rmSync(workRoot, { recursive: true, force: true }); fs.rmSync(src, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
99|
100|it("unwritable work root -> generic throw inside the started->prompted window", async () => {
101|  fs.chmodSync(workRoot, 0o500); // read-only
102|  await assert.rejects(prepareWorkdir({ localPath: src, workRoot, taskId: "t1" }));
103|  fs.chmodSync(workRoot, 0o700);
104|});
105|
106|it("git-level fault (src is not a repo and no remote) -> throws before any harness work", async () => {
107|  await assert.rejects(prepareWorkdir({ localPath: src, workRoot, taskId: "t1" }));
108|});
109|```
110|
111|(Use `localRepo()` from `runner/project.test.js` for the success control.)
112|These pin that any setup fault surfaces as a fast, pre-`prompted` failure —
113|matching the observed signature. On 0.2.0 the daemon attaches the message as
114|the interrupt reason (`runner/daemon.js:2441`); on deployed 0.1.0 it was bare.
115|
116|Run: `node --test runner/project.setupFaults.test.js`
117|
118|## 4. Prod-only verification
119|
120|`PROD-ONLY — DO NOT RUN WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION` (all read-only, but
121|on prod hosts/API; the local-alpha host is the backend box 192.168.1.206):
122|
123|```bash
124|# E1 — the deciding evidence: local-alpha daemon journal for the exhibit windows
125|# (run on 192.168.1.206 as user server; find the unit first):
126|systemctl --user list-units --type=service | grep -i runner
127|journalctl --user -u kainbain-runner-local-alpha --since '2026-11-19 12:00' --until '2026-11-19 12:45' \
128|  | grep -E 'Runner failed|restart counter|Main process exited' | tail -40
129|journalctl --user -u kainbain-runner-local-alpha --since '2026-11-20 15:30' --until '2026-11-20 15:50' | tail -60
130|journalctl --user -u kainbain-runner-local-alpha --since '2026-11-21 10:00' --until '2026-11-21 13:45' | tail -40
131|
132|# E6 — fleet versions (read-only API) and the before/after recount after 0.2.x rollout:
133|curl -s http://192.168.1.206:3100/runners | jq '.[] | {id, version, buildCommit}'
134|curl -s 'http://192.168.1.206:3100/tasks?projectId=0fd41821' | jq '[.[] | .id]'   # then per-task:
135|curl -s 'http://192.168.1.206:3100/tasks/c5c465c4?projectId=0fd41821' \
136|  | jq '[.history[] | .action] | group_by(.) | map({action: .[0], n: length}) | sort_by(-.n)'
137|```
138|
139|`PROD-ACTION — DO NOT RUN WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION`: a full e2e repro
140|would mean letting a real runner claim a real task against the live backend
141|(e.g. manually resuming a parked task like `7f6220c3`, or filling local-alpha's
142|work root). If a human wants this, the safe-ish variant is a **fully local
143|scratch stack**: `docker compose up` a dev backend on localhost, register a
144|local runner against it, create a scratch project, fill the runner work root
145|with 5 fresh `kb-*` dirs, and watch the task history — no prod involved, but
146|it still invokes a real agent, so treat it as opt-in.
147|
148|## 5. Evidence to collect when reproduced
149|
150|- local-alpha journal `Runner failed: <exact message>` lines for the window —
151|  this is the only place the root fault is named on 0.1.0.
152|- Restart-counter deltas (crash loop vs in-process re-claim loop).
153|- Backend: per-task `started` -> interrupt deltas (median ~4.7 s fleet-wide)
154|  and the absence of `prompted`.
155|- Runner build provenance (`GET /runners`) before/after the 0.2.x rollout, and
156|  the recount of bare interrupts (should drop to ~0 once reasons ship).
