2|name: kainbain-task-analysis
3|description: How to analyse live and past KainBain tasks in production — where task folders live, where every log lives (service logs, deploy log, session transcripts, per-task log entries), and how to inspect a task's state, history, reports, and failure reasons via the filesystem and the live API/WebSocket. Use when asked to investigate a task, debug a failed stage, trace a deploy, or audit what an agent did.
4|lastUpdated: 2026-10-29
5|---
6|
7|# KainBain Task Analysis (production)
8|
9|This skill teaches an agent how to investigate **live** and **past** KainBain
10|tasks in a production deployment. It covers the two things you almost always
11|need first: **where the task folder is** and **where the logs are**. Everything
12|else is reading those artifacts.
13|
14|KainBain is an AI task orchestrator. Tasks are created into a project's
15|workflow, advance through stages (`agent`, `human`, `ci`, `merge`), and are
16|persisted as markdown on disk. (Legacy `review` stages read as `human`, and
17|legacy `script` / `deploy` stages read as `ci` — a deploy command is an
18|ordinary CI stage now.) Agent stages run on **Runners**: the backend curates
19|the stage prompt and a Runner executes it in a per-task worktree, syncing
20|task docs/assets in and rewriting the backend cwd prefix to the worktree.
21|The API is Fastify; the frontend is served from the same origin. Production
22|is either Docker Compose (`docker compose up -d`, `https://<app-host>`) or a
23|native self-host where the app runs as a systemd **user** service.
24|
25|---
26|
27|## 1. Example deployment profiles (illustrative, optional)
28|
29|| | Dev | Production |
30|| --- | --- | --- |
31|| Repo / project cwd | `{{projectCwd}}` | same repo, but the *deployed* copy is `{{deployDir}}` |
32|| API base | `{{kbApiBase}}` (or `PORT` env) | the public URL / service `PORT` (override `{{kbApiBase}}` — localhost is dev-only) |
33|| Service | none (run manually) | Docker Compose service, or `<service-unit>` (systemd **user** unit on native self-hosts) |
34|| App URL | `{{kbApiBase}}` | `https://<app-host>` |
35|| Task folders | `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/` | same layout, under the project's `cwd` |
36|| Agent execution | embedded (in-process) | Runner worktree (`kb-<taskId>`, cwd prefix retargeted) |
37|
38|**Key fact:** task folders are written under the **project's `cwd`**, not under
39|`{{deployDir}}`. The project's `cwd` is recorded in
40|`<project cwd>/.kainbain/project.json` (e.g. `"cwd": "{{projectCwd}}"`).
41|Tasks live at:
42|
43|```text
44|{{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>/
45|```
46|
47|`{{deployDir}}` is only the *deployed build* (api + frontend/dist + build.json);
48|it does **not** hold task data. Don't look for tasks there.
49|
50|---
51|
52|## 2. The task folder (the single most important artifact)
53|
54|Every task is a directory under `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/`:
55|
56|```text
57|docs/tasks/<taskId>/
58|├── task.md                      # canonical task entity (frontmatter + body)
59|├── IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md       # plan written by the Plan stage (if used)
60|├── plan-<timestamp>.md          # stage report: Plan (only if the stage opted in)
61|├── <stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md  # failure report (ALWAYS written on stage failure)
62|├── automated-tests-<timestamp>.md # CI / human-checkpoint report (always written)
63|└── ...                          # one report per stage run that produced one
64|```
65|
66|**Reporting is opt-in for agent stages.** A default agent stage writes NO
67|report on success — no agent-authored summary file and no engine-generated
68|one. A stage opts in via `report: true` on the stage config or by attaching
69|the `stage-report` skill. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
70|are always written on stage failure, and CI stages (including legacy
71|`script` / `deploy` commands) and merge stages and human checkpoints always
72|write their own reports.
73|
74|### `task.md` — the canonical record
75|
76|`task.md` is the authoritative, server-written snapshot of the task. Read it
77|first. It has YAML frontmatter and a markdown body:
78|
79|- **Frontmatter:** `id`, `projectId`, `workflowId`, `title`, `status`,
80|  `currentStageId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `enteredStageAt`, `timeInStage`,
81|  `outputReport`, `feedback`, `blockedBy` (plus machine fields such as
82|  `branch`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`).
83|- **`# Goal`** — the task's goal/title.
84|- **`# History`** — an append-only audit trail, one line per event:
85|  `- <ISO timestamp>: <action>` (created, edited, stage advanced, failed, etc.).
86|  This is the fastest way to reconstruct what happened and when.
87|- **`# Timeline`** — one line per stage visit (`<timestamp>: <stage> |
88|  <status> | <duration>`, with a diff stat when the stage touched git).
89|- **`# Log Entries`** — the stored per-task log as structured JSON, capped at
90|  `KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT` entries (default 500, oldest evicted under
91|  a marker). This is the single bound on task log storage. (Very old files may
92|  still carry a rendered `# Process Logs` section instead — legacy files are
93|  parsed back into entries on load.)
94|- `KAINBAIN_PROCESS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (default 32000) only bounds one stage's
95|  captured streamed output kept in memory **while it runs** — it is not the
96|  stored task log.
97|
98|### Stage report files (`<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`, `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
99|
100|Agent-stage success reports are **opt-in** (stage `report: true` or the
101|`stage-report` skill). Failure reports always exist and carry the `-failure-`
102|filename infix. Auto-generated reports carry the marker
103|`<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->` (hidden in most renderers).
104|A report contains: task, stage type, model, duration, status (PASSED/FAILED),
105|summary of changes, execution output, modified files, and verification status.
106|On failure it includes the error and notes the fallback routing.
107|
108|### `docs/tasks/active/`
109|
110|A separate, manually-maintained scratch area (`docs/tasks/active/<taskId>/N.md`)
111|holds working notes per stage. It is **not** written by the API — treat it as
112|human scratch, not authoritative.
113|
114|---
115|
116|## 3. Where the logs live
117|
118|There are **four** distinct log sources. Match the question to the source.
119|
120|### 3a. Service / request logs — container logs or systemd journal
121|
122|The production API logs Fastify structured JSON (`level`, `time`, `pid`,
123|`req`, `res`, `msg`). Where to read it depends on the deployment shape:
124|
125|```bash
126|# Docker Compose deployment
127|docker compose logs -f backend     # tail live service logs
128|docker compose logs --tail 200 backend
129|docker compose ps                  # confirm the service is up
130|
131|# Native self-host (systemd user unit)
132|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -f
133|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -n 200
134|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> --since "2026-10-29 08:00:00"
135|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 100
136|systemctl --user status <service-unit>
137|systemctl --user restart <service-unit>
138|```
139|
140|Use this for: request failures, startup crashes, unhandled errors, and
141|confirming the service is up. On a native self-host the unit file is
142|typically at `~/.config/systemd/user/<service-unit>` (WorkingDirectory
143|`{{deployDir}}/api`, `PORT` set to the API port, `NODE_ENV=production`).
144|
145|### 3b. Deploy logs — `<deploy-state-dir>/`
146|
147|Self-deployment state and logs live under the deploy state directory
148|(typically `~/.kainbain/deploy/` when self-hosting KainBain):
149|
150|```text
151|<deploy-state-dir>/
152|├── deploy.log        # full deploy script output (append-only)
153|├── state.json        # current deploy state
154|├── last-result.json  # last deploy result
155|├── history.jsonl     # append-only deploy history (one JSON per line)
156|├── build.txt         # autoincrementing build counter
157|├── deploy.lock       # flock lock file
158|└── releases/         # per-build release snapshots
159|```
160|
161|The live build number is stamped into `{{deployDir}}/build.json`
162|(`{ buildNumber, deployedAt, commit }`). The header shows `#B<number>` — clicking
163|it opens the KainBain changelog baked into the deploy (`{{deployDir}}/changelog.json`,
164|latest 200 commits on the default branch plus `totalCount`). On Docker
165|deployments the build files live inside the image, not on the host — use the
166|API (`GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/changelog`) instead of host paths.
167|
168|```bash
169|tail -n 200 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
170|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
171|cat <deploy-state-dir>/state.json
172|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
173|```
174|
175|Use this for: "did the deploy succeed / what build is live / why did it roll
176|back". The API also exposes these via `GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/log`,
177|`POST /deploy`, `POST /deploy/rollback`, plus `GET /deploy/changelog` for the
178|baked history (`{ changelog: null, reason: "not-baked" }` before the first
179|deploy that bakes it).
180|
181|### 3c. Agent session transcripts — worktree (Runner) or `.kainbain/sessions/` (embedded)
182|
183|Runner-executed stages keep their session where the harness ran: the
184|per-task worktree on the **Runner host** (`sessionDir` = the worktree), not on
185|the backend. Only embedded (non-Runner) runs write transcripts to the
186|backend's `<project cwd>/.kainbain/sessions/` — one JSONL transcript per
187|session (one JSON object per line): `session`, `model_change`,
188|`thinking_level_change`, and message/tool events, resumed via the SDK's
189|`SessionManager`.
190|
191|```bash
192|ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/
193|head -5 {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/*.jsonl
194|```
195|
196|Use this for: the raw agent conversation / model used / thinking level for a
197|project. Always check **which host ran the stage** first — for Runner tasks
198|the transcript is on the Runner host, and the backend directory may not have
199|it. Note: `.kainbain/` is gitignored, so these are local-only.
200|
201|### 3d. Per-task logs — `# Log Entries` in `task.md`, Live Console on the wire
202|
203|The stored agent/tool/CI output for a task is the `# Log Entries` section of
204|`task.md` (see §2). Live output streams over the WebSocket as `PROCESS_STDOUT`
205|/ `process:stdout` frames, which is what the UI's Live Console renders — for a
206|running task, watch the socket (see §4b), not the file. `task.md` is
207|rewritten on every state change, so its frontmatter, `# History`, and
208|`# Log Entries` stay current, but there is no rendered process-log tail to
209|`tail -f` anymore.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 4. Analysing a **live** task
214|
215|A "live" task is one currently executing or queued. The engine is a single
216|global executor (`ExecutionQueue`) with an `engineState` snapshot.
217|
218|### 4a. Via the API (fastest, no filesystem)
219|
220|```bash
221|# Engine state: what is running right now
222|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
223|
224|# Full observability: engine + health + build + task metrics
225|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
226|
227|# Health
228|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
229|
230|# List tasks for a project (projectId optional → active project)
231|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
232|
233|# Single task (full state incl. history, reports, log entries)
234|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/<taskId>?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
235|
236|# Task queue
237|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/queue?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
238|
239|# Session status (active, streaming, message count, disk session)
240|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/session/status?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
241|```
242|
243|`GET /status/observability` returns `engine` (status, activeTaskId,
244|activeStageId, activeStageName, activeStageType), `build`, `health`, and
245|`observability` (totals: completed/failed/running/waitingHuman/paused/blocked,
246|plus recent completed/failed lists with failure reasons).
247|
248|### 4b. Via WebSocket (live streaming)
249|
250|The frontend subscribes to `GET /ws?projectId=<projectId>` (WebSocket upgrade).
251|Events are JSON `{ type, sessionId, payload, timestamp }`. Key types:
252|`CONNECTED`, `ENGINE_STATE`, `TASK_UPDATED`, `TASK_DELETED`, `NOTIFICATION`,
253|`PROCESS_STDOUT` / `process:stdout`, and agent events (`agent_start`,
254|`tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`,
255|`message_update`, `error`). The UI's **Live Console** (Observability dashboard)
256|renders these with severity tags (`AGENT`, `CI`, `ERROR`, `HUMAN`, `TOOL`).
257|
258|To watch live from a script, connect to the WebSocket endpoint at
259|`{{kbApiBase}}/ws?projectId=<id>` (upgrade `http`→`ws` / `https`→`wss`) and log
260|incoming frames.
261|
262|### 4c. Via the filesystem
263|
264|For a live task, `task.md` is rewritten on every state change, so
265|`tail -f docs/tasks/<taskId>/task.md` shows frontmatter, `# History`, and
266|`# Log Entries` growing in near-real-time (watch the WebSocket for the
267|live stream itself — see §3d). The `status` frontmatter tells you where it
268|is: `running_agent`, `running_ci`, `running_merge`, `advancing`, `in_stage`,
269|`waiting_human`, `paused`, `failed`, `completed` (`interrupted` after an
270|unclean restart; `running_deploy` is a legacy label from before the deploy
271|runtime was removed). Note: with Runner execution, absolute backend-cwd paths
272|in prompts are retargeted to the task worktree — resolve worktree-relative
273|paths against `kb-<taskId>`, not the backend checkout.
274|
275|---
276|
277|## 5. Analysing a **past** task
278|
279|A "past" task is one that completed, failed, or was parked. Everything you need
280|is on disk — no live service required.
281|
282|1. **Find the task folder.** List task dirs, newest first:
283|
284|   ```bash
285|   ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/
286|   ```
287|
288|   Or find by title/status:
289|
290|   ```bash
291|   grep -rl "status: \"failed\"" {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/*/task.md
292|   ```
293|
294|2. **Read `task.md`** — frontmatter gives status, current stage, timestamps;
295|   `# History` gives the full event timeline; `# Timeline` gives per-stage
296|   durations; `# Log Entries` gives the stored output.
297|
298|3. **Read the stage reports** in the same folder — one per stage run that
299|   produced one (opt-in agent stages + all failure reports), in
300|   filename-timestamp order. They tell you what each stage produced and
301|   whether it passed or failed. Failure reports use the `-failure-` infix.
302|   For stages that did NOT opt in, reconstruct from `# Log Entries`, the
303|   session transcript (worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/`
304|   for embedded runs), and the git history.
305|
306|4. **Reconstruct the failure.** For a failed task, check:
307|   - `status: "failed"` in frontmatter.
308|   - The last `# History` entries (e.g. `Stage failed: <reason>`).
309|   - The FAILED stage report (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`; contains
310|     the error and fallback routing).
311|   - `# Log Entries` tail for the actual error output.
312|   - The API's observability `recentFailed` list (if the service is up) for
313|     `failureReason` / `lastError`.
314|
315|5. **Cross-check the deploy** (if the task reached a deploy command — deploys
316|   run as ordinary CI stages now): see `<deploy-state-dir>/history.jsonl`
317|   and `last-result.json` for whether the deploy succeeded and which build
318|   went live.
319|
320|---
321|
322|## 6. Common analysis recipes
323|
324|### "Why did this task fail?"
325|
326|```bash
327|TASK={{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>
328|grep -E "status|currentStageId" "$TASK/task.md"          # where it ended
329|grep -E "^- " "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20                 # last history events
330|grep -rl "FAILED" "$TASK"/*-failure-*.md                  # failed stage reports
331|grep -E "Log Entries" -A 5 "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20    # stored log tail
332|```
333|
334|### "What is running right now?"
335|
336|```bash
337|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
338|```
339|
340|### "Did the last deploy work / what build is live?"
341|
342|```bash
343|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
344|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
345|tail -n 50 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
346|```
347|
348|### "What did the agent actually do in stage X?"
349|
350|Read any stage report `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md` or
351|`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md` (summary, output, modified files) plus
352|the `# Log Entries` section of `task.md`. Agent stages that did not opt into
353|reporting leave no success report — use the session transcript (Runner
354|worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs) and
355|git log.
356|
357|### "Is the service healthy?"
358|
359|```bash
360|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
361|docker compose logs --tail 50 backend          # Docker deployment
362|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 50   # native self-host
363|```
364|
365|---
366|
367|## 7. Gotchas
368|
369|- **Task data is under the project `cwd`, not `{{deployDir}}`.** The deployed
370|  build dir only holds code + `build.json`.
371|- **`task.md` is a snapshot, not a full transcript.** Stored logs are capped
372|  (`KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT`, default 500 entries, oldest evicted under
373|  a marker). For the full agent conversation use the session transcript —
374|  Runner worktree on the Runner host, or the session JSONL in
375|  `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs.
376|- **`.kainbain/` is gitignored** — session transcripts and deploy state are
377|  local-only, not in the repo. Runner worktrees (`kb-<taskId>`) are also
378|  local to the Runner host.
379|- **Absolute backend paths are retargeted on Runners.** The backend curates
380|  prompts with its own project cwd and the Runner rewrites that prefix to
381|  the prepared worktree — a path that exists on the backend may live under
382|  the worktree on the Runner host.
383|- **There is no `deploy` stage type anymore.** Legacy `deploy` (like `script`)
384|  reads as `ci`; merge-plus-deploy composites are migrated into a git-only
385|  merge stage plus a dedicated CI stage. `running_deploy` in old records is a
386|  legacy label.
387|- **`docs/tasks/active/` is human scratch**, not API-written. Don't treat it as
388|  authoritative.
389|- **Auto-generated reports** are marked with
390|  `<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->`; distinguish them from manual ones.
391|- **Agent-stage success reports are opt-in.** A default agent stage that
392|  succeeded leaves NO report file — absence of a `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`
393|  is expected, not data loss. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
394|  are always written.
395|- **The engine is single-threaded** (one global `ExecutionQueue`). Only one
396|  task executes at a time; others queue. `engine.status` is `idle` when nothing
397|  runs.
398|- **Interrupted tasks** (server restart mid-run) are rehydrated with status
399|  `interrupted` and a history entry "Execution recovered after server restart".
400|- **Auto-iteration:** a failed stage may auto re-run (fix → re-test → re-review)
401|  up to `KAINBAIN_MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS` (default 8) before being parked as
402|  `failed`. Each failed attempt leaves a `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`
403|  report; multiple failure files for the same stage = auto-iteration attempts.

7|# KainBain Task Analysis (production)
8|
9|This skill teaches an agent how to investigate **live** and **past** KainBain
10|tasks in a production deployment. It covers the two things you almost always
11|need first: **where the task folder is** and **where the logs are**. Everything
12|else is reading those artifacts.
13|
14|KainBain is an AI task orchestrator. Tasks are created into a project's
15|workflow, advance through stages (`agent`, `human`, `ci`, `merge`), and are
16|persisted as markdown on disk. (Legacy `review` stages read as `human`, and
17|legacy `script` / `deploy` stages read as `ci` — a deploy command is an
18|ordinary CI stage now.) Agent stages run on **Runners**: the backend curates
19|the stage prompt and a Runner executes it in a per-task worktree, syncing
20|task docs/assets in and rewriting the backend cwd prefix to the worktree.
21|The API is Fastify; the frontend is served from the same origin. Production
22|is either Docker Compose (`docker compose up -d`, `https://<app-host>`) or a
23|native self-host where the app runs as a systemd **user** service.
24|
25|---
26|
27|## 1. Example deployment profiles (illustrative, optional)
28|
29|| | Dev | Production |
30|| --- | --- | --- |
31|| Repo / project cwd | `{{projectCwd}}` | same repo, but the *deployed* copy is `{{deployDir}}` |
32|| API base | `{{kbApiBase}}` (or `PORT` env) | the public URL / service `PORT` (override `{{kbApiBase}}` — localhost is dev-only) |
33|| Service | none (run manually) | Docker Compose service, or `<service-unit>` (systemd **user** unit on native self-hosts) |
34|| App URL | `{{kbApiBase}}` | `https://<app-host>` |
35|| Task folders | `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/` | same layout, under the project's `cwd` |
36|| Agent execution | embedded (in-process) | Runner worktree (`kb-<taskId>`, cwd prefix retargeted) |
37|
38|**Key fact:** task folders are written under the **project's `cwd`**, not under
39|`{{deployDir}}`. The project's `cwd` is recorded in
40|`<project cwd>/.kainbain/project.json` (e.g. `"cwd": "{{projectCwd}}"`).
41|Tasks live at:
42|
43|```text
44|{{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>/
45|```
46|
47|`{{deployDir}}` is only the *deployed build* (api + frontend/dist + build.json);
48|it does **not** hold task data. Don't look for tasks there.
49|
50|---
51|
52|## 2. The task folder (the single most important artifact)
53|
54|Every task is a directory under `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/`:
55|
56|```text
57|docs/tasks/<taskId>/
58|├── task.md                      # canonical task entity (frontmatter + body)
59|├── IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md       # plan written by the Plan stage (if used)
60|├── plan-<timestamp>.md          # stage report: Plan (only if the stage opted in)
61|├── <stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md  # failure report (ALWAYS written on stage failure)
62|├── automated-tests-<timestamp>.md # CI / human-checkpoint report (always written)
63|└── ...                          # one report per stage run that produced one
64|```
65|
66|**Reporting is opt-in for agent stages.** A default agent stage writes NO
67|report on success — no agent-authored summary file and no engine-generated
68|one. A stage opts in via `report: true` on the stage config or by attaching
69|the `stage-report` skill. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
70|are always written on stage failure, and CI stages (including legacy
71|`script` / `deploy` commands) and merge stages and human checkpoints always
72|write their own reports.
73|
74|### `task.md` — the canonical record
75|
76|`task.md` is the authoritative, server-written snapshot of the task. Read it
77|first. It has YAML frontmatter and a markdown body:
78|
79|- **Frontmatter:** `id`, `projectId`, `workflowId`, `title`, `status`,
80|  `currentStageId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `enteredStageAt`, `timeInStage`,
81|  `outputReport`, `feedback`, `blockedBy` (plus machine fields such as
82|  `branch`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`).
83|- **`# Goal`** — the task's goal/title.
84|- **`# History`** — an append-only audit trail, one line per event:
85|  `- <ISO timestamp>: <action>` (created, edited, stage advanced, failed, etc.).
86|  This is the fastest way to reconstruct what happened and when.
87|- **`# Timeline`** — one line per stage visit (`<timestamp>: <stage> |
88|  <status> | <duration>`, with a diff stat when the stage touched git).
89|- **`# Log Entries`** — the stored per-task log as structured JSON, capped at
90|  `KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT` entries (default 500, oldest evicted under
91|  a marker). This is the single bound on task log storage. (Very old files may
92|  still carry a rendered `# Process Logs` section instead — legacy files are
93|  parsed back into entries on load.)
94|- `KAINBAIN_PROCESS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (default 32000) only bounds one stage's
95|  captured streamed output kept in memory **while it runs** — it is not the
96|  stored task log.
97|
98|### Stage report files (`<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`, `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
99|
100|Agent-stage success reports are **opt-in** (stage `report: true` or the
101|`stage-report` skill). Failure reports always exist and carry the `-failure-`
102|filename infix. Auto-generated reports carry the marker
103|`<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->` (hidden in most renderers).
104|A report contains: task, stage type, model, duration, status (PASSED/FAILED),
105|summary of changes, execution output, modified files, and verification status.
106|On failure it includes the error and notes the fallback routing.
107|
108|### `docs/tasks/active/`
109|
110|A separate, manually-maintained scratch area (`docs/tasks/active/<taskId>/N.md`)
111|holds working notes per stage. It is **not** written by the API — treat it as
112|human scratch, not authoritative.
113|

188|`thinking_level_change`, and message/tool events, resumed via the SDK's
189|`SessionManager`.
190|
191|```bash
192|ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/
193|head -5 {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/*.jsonl
194|```
195|
196|Use this for: the raw agent conversation / model used / thinking level for a
197|project. Always check **which host ran the stage** first — for Runner tasks
198|the transcript is on the Runner host, and the backend directory may not have
199|it. Note: `.kainbain/` is gitignored, so these are local-only.
200|
201|### 3d. Per-task logs — `# Log Entries` in `task.md`, Live Console on the wire
202|
203|The stored agent/tool/CI output for a task is the `# Log Entries` section of
204|`task.md` (see §2). Live output streams over the WebSocket as `PROCESS_STDOUT`
205|/ `process:stdout` frames, which is what the UI's Live Console renders — for a
206|running task, watch the socket (see §4b), not the file. `task.md` is
207|rewritten on every state change, so its frontmatter, `# History`, and
208|`# Log Entries` stay current, but there is no rendered process-log tail to
209|`tail -f` anymore.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 4. Analysing a **live** task
214|
215|A "live" task is one currently executing or queued. The engine is a single
216|global executor (`ExecutionQueue`) with an `engineState` snapshot.
217|
218|### 4a. Via the API (fastest, no filesystem)
219|
220|```bash
221|# Engine state: what is running right now
222|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
223|
224|# Full observability: engine + health + build + task metrics
225|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
226|
227|# Health
228|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
229|
230|# List tasks for a project (projectId optional → active project)
231|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
232|
233|# Single task (full state incl. history, reports, log entries)
234|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/<taskId>?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
235|
236|# Task queue
237|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/queue?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
238|
239|# Session status (active, streaming, message count, disk session)
240|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/session/status?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
241|```
242|
243|`GET /status/observability` returns `engine` (status, activeTaskId,
244|activeStageId, activeStageName, activeStageType), `build`, `health`, and
245|`observability` (totals: completed/failed/running/waitingHuman/paused/blocked,
246|plus recent completed/failed lists with failure reasons).
247|
248|### 4b. Via WebSocket (live streaming)
249|
250|The frontend subscribes to `GET /ws?projectId=<projectId>` (WebSocket upgrade).
251|Events are JSON `{ type, sessionId, payload, timestamp }`. Key types:
252|`CONNECTED`, `ENGINE_STATE`, `TASK_UPDATED`, `TASK_DELETED`, `NOTIFICATION`,
253|`PROCESS_STDOUT` / `process:stdout`, and agent events (`agent_start`,
254|`tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`,
255|`message_update`, `error`). The UI's **Live Console** (Observability dashboard)
256|renders these with severity tags (`AGENT`, `CI`, `ERROR`, `HUMAN`, `TOOL`).
257|
258|To watch live from a script, connect to the WebSocket endpoint at
259|`{{kbApiBase}}/ws?projectId=<id>` (upgrade `http`→`ws` / `https`→`wss`) and log
260|incoming frames.
261|
262|### 4c. Via the filesystem
263|
264|For a live task, `task.md` is rewritten on every state change, so
265|`tail -f docs/tasks/<taskId>/task.md` shows frontmatter, `# History`, and
266|`# Log Entries` growing in near-real-time (watch the WebSocket for the
267|live stream itself — see §3d). The `status` frontmatter tells you where it
268|is: `running_agent`, `running_ci`, `running_merge`, `advancing`, `in_stage`,
269|`waiting_human`, `paused`, `failed`, `completed` (`interrupted` after an
270|unclean restart; `running_deploy` is a legacy label from before the deploy
271|runtime was removed). Note: with Runner execution, absolute backend-cwd paths
272|in prompts are retargeted to the task worktree — resolve worktree-relative
273|paths against `kb-<taskId>`, not the backend checkout.
274|
275|---
276|
277|## 5. Analysing a **past** task
278|
279|A "past" task is one that completed, failed, or was parked. Everything you need
280|is on disk — no live service required.
281|
282|1. **Find the task folder.** List task dirs, newest first:
283|
284|   ```bash
285|   ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/
286|   ```
287|
288|   Or find by title/status:
289|
290|   ```bash
291|   grep -rl "status: \"failed\"" {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/*/task.md
292|   ```
293|
294|2. **Read `task.md`** — frontmatter gives status, current stage, timestamps;
295|   `# History` gives the full event timeline; `# Timeline` gives per-stage
296|   durations; `# Log Entries` gives the stored output.
297|
298|3. **Read the stage reports** in the same folder — one per stage run that
299|   produced one (opt-in agent stages + all failure reports), in
300|   filename-timestamp order. They tell you what each stage produced and
301|   whether it passed or failed. Failure reports use the `-failure-` infix.
302|   For stages that did NOT opt in, reconstruct from `# Log Entries`, the
303|   session transcript (worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/`
304|   for embedded runs), and the git history.
305|
306|4. **Reconstruct the failure.** For a failed task, check:
307|   - `status: "failed"` in frontmatter.
308|   - The last `# History` entries (e.g. `Stage failed: <reason>`).
309|   - The FAILED stage report (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`; contains
310|     the error and fallback routing).
311|   - `# Log Entries` tail for the actual error output.
312|   - The API's observability `recentFailed` list (if the service is up) for
313|     `failureReason` / `lastError`.
314|
315|5. **Cross-check the deploy** (if the task reached a deploy command — deploys
316|   run as ordinary CI stages now): see `<deploy-state-dir>/history.jsonl`
317|   and `last-result.json` for whether the deploy succeeded and which build
318|   went live.
319|
320|---
321|
322|## 6. Common analysis recipes
323|
324|### "Why did this task fail?"
325|
326|```bash
327|TASK={{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>
328|grep -E "status|currentStageId" "$TASK/task.md"          # where it ended
329|grep -E "^- " "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20                 # last history events
330|grep -rl "FAILED" "$TASK"/*-failure-*.md                  # failed stage reports
331|grep -E "Log Entries" -A 5 "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20    # stored log tail
332|```
333|
334|### "What is running right now?"
335|
336|```bash
337|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
338|```
339|
340|### "Did the last deploy work / what build is live?"
341|
342|```bash
343|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
344|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
345|tail -n 50 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
346|```
347|
348|### "What did the agent actually do in stage X?"
349|
350|Read any stage report `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md` or
351|`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md` (summary, output, modified files) plus
352|the `# Log Entries` section of `task.md`. Agent stages that did not opt into
353|reporting leave no success report — use the session transcript (Runner
354|worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs) and
355|git log.
356|
357|### "Is the service healthy?"
358|
359|```bash
360|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
361|docker compose logs --tail 50 backend          # Docker deployment
362|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 50   # native self-host
363|```
364|
365|---
366|
367|## 7. Gotchas
368|
369|- **Task data is under the project `cwd`, not `{{deployDir}}`.** The deployed
370|  build dir only holds code + `build.json`.
371|- **`task.md` is a snapshot, not a full transcript.** Stored logs are capped
372|  (`KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT`, default 500 entries, oldest evicted under
373|  a marker). For the full agent conversation use the session transcript —
374|  Runner worktree on the Runner host, or the session JSONL in
375|  `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs.
376|- **`.kainbain/` is gitignored** — session transcripts and deploy state are
377|  local-only, not in the repo. Runner worktrees (`kb-<taskId>`) are also
378|  local to the Runner host.
379|- **Absolute backend paths are retargeted on Runners.** The backend curates
380|  prompts with its own project cwd and the Runner rewrites that prefix to
381|  the prepared worktree — a path that exists on the backend may live under
382|  the worktree on the Runner host.
383|- **There is no `deploy` stage type anymore.** Legacy `deploy` (like `script`)
384|  reads as `ci`; merge-plus-deploy composites are migrated into a git-only
385|  merge stage plus a dedicated CI stage. `running_deploy` in old records is a
386|  legacy label.
387|- **`docs/tasks/active/` is human scratch**, not API-written. Don't treat it as
388|  authoritative.
389|- **Auto-generated reports** are marked with
390|  `<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->`; distinguish them from manual ones.
391|- **Agent-stage success reports are opt-in.** A default agent stage that
392|  succeeded leaves NO report file — absence of a `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`
393|  is expected, not data loss. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
394|  are always written.
395|- **The engine is single-threaded** (one global `ExecutionQueue`). Only one
396|  task executes at a time; others queue. `engine.status` is `idle` when nothing
397|  runs.
398|- **Interrupted tasks** (server restart mid-run) are rehydrated with status
399|  `interrupted` and a history entry "Execution recovered after server restart".
400|- **Auto-iteration:** a failed stage may auto re-run (fix → re-test → re-review)
401|  up to `KAINBAIN_MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS` (default 8) before being parked as
402|  `failed`. Each failed attempt leaves a `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`
403|  report; multiple failure files for the same stage = auto-iteration attempts.

7|# KainBain Task Analysis (production)
8|
9|This skill teaches an agent how to investigate **live** and **past** KainBain
10|tasks in a production deployment. It covers the two things you almost always
11|need first: **where the task folder is** and **where the logs are**. Everything
12|else is reading those artifacts.
13|
14|KainBain is an AI task orchestrator. Tasks are created into a project's
15|workflow, advance through stages (`agent`, `human`, `ci`, `merge`), and are
16|persisted as markdown on disk. (Legacy `review` stages read as `human`, and
17|legacy `script` / `deploy` stages read as `ci` — a deploy command is an
18|ordinary CI stage now.) Agent stages run on **Runners**: the backend curates
19|the stage prompt and a Runner executes it in a per-task worktree, syncing
20|task docs/assets in and rewriting the backend cwd prefix to the worktree.
21|The API is Fastify; the frontend is served from the same origin. Production
22|is either Docker Compose (`docker compose up -d`, `https://<app-host>`) or a
23|native self-host where the app runs as a systemd **user** service.
24|
25|---
26|
27|## 1. Example deployment profiles (illustrative, optional)
28|
29|| | Dev | Production |
30|| --- | --- | --- |
31|| Repo / project cwd | `{{projectCwd}}` | same repo, but the *deployed* copy is `{{deployDir}}` |
32|| API base | `{{kbApiBase}}` (or `PORT` env) | the public URL / service `PORT` (override `{{kbApiBase}}` — localhost is dev-only) |
33|| Service | none (run manually) | Docker Compose service, or `<service-unit>` (systemd **user** unit on native self-hosts) |
34|| App URL | `{{kbApiBase}}` | `https://<app-host>` |
35|| Task folders | `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/` | same layout, under the project's `cwd` |
36|| Agent execution | embedded (in-process) | Runner worktree (`kb-<taskId>`, cwd prefix retargeted) |
37|
38|**Key fact:** task folders are written under the **project's `cwd`**, not under
39|`{{deployDir}}`. The project's `cwd` is recorded in
40|`<project cwd>/.kainbain/project.json` (e.g. `"cwd": "{{projectCwd}}"`).
41|Tasks live at:
42|
43|```text
44|{{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>/
45|```
46|
47|`{{deployDir}}` is only the *deployed build* (api + frontend/dist + build.json);
48|it does **not** hold task data. Don't look for tasks there.
49|
50|---
51|
52|## 2. The task folder (the single most important artifact)
53|
54|Every task is a directory under `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/`:
55|
56|```text
57|docs/tasks/<taskId>/
58|├── task.md                      # canonical task entity (frontmatter + body)
59|├── IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md       # plan written by the Plan stage (if used)
60|├── plan-<timestamp>.md          # stage report: Plan (only if the stage opted in)
61|├── <stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md  # failure report (ALWAYS written on stage failure)
62|├── automated-tests-<timestamp>.md # CI / human-checkpoint report (always written)
63|└── ...                          # one report per stage run that produced one
64|```
65|
66|**Reporting is opt-in for agent stages.** A default agent stage writes NO
67|report on success — no agent-authored summary file and no engine-generated
68|one. A stage opts in via `report: true` on the stage config or by attaching
69|the `stage-report` skill. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
70|are always written on stage failure, and CI stages (including legacy
71|`script` / `deploy` commands) and merge stages and human checkpoints always
72|write their own reports.
73|
74|### `task.md` — the canonical record
75|
76|`task.md` is the authoritative, server-written snapshot of the task. Read it
77|first. It has YAML frontmatter and a markdown body:
78|
79|- **Frontmatter:** `id`, `projectId`, `workflowId`, `title`, `status`,
80|  `currentStageId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `enteredStageAt`, `timeInStage`,
81|  `outputReport`, `feedback`, `blockedBy` (plus machine fields such as
82|  `branch`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`).
83|- **`# Goal`** — the task's goal/title.
84|- **`# History`** — an append-only audit trail, one line per event:
85|  `- <ISO timestamp>: <action>` (created, edited, stage advanced, failed, etc.).
86|  This is the fastest way to reconstruct what happened and when.
87|- **`# Timeline`** — one line per stage visit (`<timestamp>: <stage> |
88|  <status> | <duration>`, with a diff stat when the stage touched git).
89|- **`# Log Entries`** — the stored per-task log as structured JSON, capped at
90|  `KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT` entries (default 500, oldest evicted under
91|  a marker). This is the single bound on task log storage. (Very old files may
92|  still carry a rendered `# Process Logs` section instead — legacy files are
93|  parsed back into entries on load.)
94|- `KAINBAIN_PROCESS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (default 32000) only bounds one stage's
95|  captured streamed output kept in memory **while it runs** — it is not the
96|  stored task log.
97|
98|### Stage report files (`<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`, `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
99|
100|Agent-stage success reports are **opt-in** (stage `report: true` or the
101|`stage-report` skill). Failure reports always exist and carry the `-failure-`
102|filename infix. Auto-generated reports carry the marker
103|`<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->` (hidden in most renderers).
104|A report contains: task, stage type, model, duration, status (PASSED/FAILED),
105|summary of changes, execution output, modified files, and verification status.
106|On failure it includes the error and notes the fallback routing.
107|
108|### `docs/tasks/active/`
109|
110|A separate, manually-maintained scratch area (`docs/tasks/active/<taskId>/N.md`)
111|holds working notes per stage. It is **not** written by the API — treat it as
112|human scratch, not authoritative.
113|
114|---
115|
116|## 3. Where the logs live
117|
118|There are **four** distinct log sources. Match the question to the source.
119|
120|### 3a. Service / request logs — container logs or systemd journal
121|
122|The production API logs Fastify structured JSON (`level`, `time`, `pid`,
123|`req`, `res`, `msg`). Where to read it depends on the deployment shape:
124|
125|```bash
126|# Docker Compose deployment
127|docker compose logs -f backend     # tail live service logs
128|docker compose logs --tail 200 backend
129|docker compose ps                  # confirm the service is up
130|
131|# Native self-host (systemd user unit)
132|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -f
133|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -n 200
134|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> --since "2026-10-29 08:00:00"
135|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 100
136|systemctl --user status <service-unit>
137|systemctl --user restart <service-unit>
138|```
139|
140|Use this for: request failures, startup crashes, unhandled errors, and
141|confirming the service is up. On a native self-host the unit file is
142|typically at `~/.config/systemd/user/<service-unit>` (WorkingDirectory
143|`{{deployDir}}/api`, `PORT` set to the API port, `NODE_ENV=production`).
144|
145|### 3b. Deploy logs — `<deploy-state-dir>/`
146|
147|Self-deployment state and logs live under the deploy state directory
148|(typically `~/.kainbain/deploy/` when self-hosting KainBain):
149|
150|```text
151|<deploy-state-dir>/
152|├── deploy.log        # full deploy script output (append-only)
153|├── state.json        # current deploy state
154|├── last-result.json  # last deploy result
155|├── history.jsonl     # append-only deploy history (one JSON per line)
156|├── build.txt         # autoincrementing build counter
157|├── deploy.lock       # flock lock file
158|└── releases/         # per-build release snapshots
159|```
160|
161|The live build number is stamped into `{{deployDir}}/build.json`
162|(`{ buildNumber, deployedAt, commit }`). The header shows `#B<number>` — clicking
163|it opens the KainBain changelog baked into the deploy (`{{deployDir}}/changelog.json`,
164|latest 200 commits on the default branch plus `totalCount`). On Docker
165|deployments the build files live inside the image, not on the host — use the
166|API (`GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/changelog`) instead of host paths.
167|
168|```bash
169|tail -n 200 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
170|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
171|cat <deploy-state-dir>/state.json
172|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
173|```
174|
175|Use this for: "did the deploy succeed / what build is live / why did it roll
176|back". The API also exposes these via `GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/log`,
177|`POST /deploy`, `POST /deploy/rollback`, plus `GET /deploy/changelog` for the
178|baked history (`{ changelog: null, reason: "not-baked" }` before the first
179|deploy that bakes it).
180|
181|### 3c. Agent session transcripts — worktree (Runner) or `.kainbain/sessions/` (embedded)
182|
183|Runner-executed stages keep their session where the harness ran: the
184|per-task worktree on the **Runner host** (`sessionDir` = the worktree), not on
185|the backend. Only embedded (non-Runner) runs write transcripts to the
186|backend's `<project cwd>/.kainbain/sessions/` — one JSONL transcript per
187|session (one JSON object per line): `session`, `model_change`,
188|`thinking_level_change`, and message/tool events, resumed via the SDK's
189|`SessionManager`.
190|
191|```bash
192|ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/
193|head -5 {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/*.jsonl
194|```
195|
196|Use this for: the raw agent conversation / model used / thinking level for a
197|project. Always check **which host ran the stage** first — for Runner tasks
198|the transcript is on the Runner host, and the backend directory may not have
199|it. Note: `.kainbain/` is gitignored, so these are local-only.
200|
201|### 3d. Per-task logs — `# Log Entries` in `task.md`, Live Console on the wire
202|
203|The stored agent/tool/CI output for a task is the `# Log Entries` section of
204|`task.md` (see §2). Live output streams over the WebSocket as `PROCESS_STDOUT`
205|/ `process:stdout` frames, which is what the UI's Live Console renders — for a

207|rewritten on every state change, so its frontmatter, `# History`, and

277|## 5. Analysing a **past** task
278|
279|A "past" task is one that completed, failed, or was parked. Everything you need
280|is on disk — no live service required.
281|
282|1. **Find the task folder.** List task dirs, newest first:
283|
284|   ```bash
285|   ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/
286|   ```
287|
288|   Or find by title/status:
289|
290|   ```bash
291|   grep -rl "status: \"failed\"" {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/*/task.md
292|   ```
293|
294|2. **Read `task.md`** — frontmatter gives status, current stage, timestamps;
295|   `# History` gives the full event timeline; `# Timeline` gives per-stage
296|   durations; `# Log Entries` gives the stored output.
297|
298|3. **Read the stage reports** in the same folder — one per stage run that
299|   produced one (opt-in agent stages + all failure reports), in
300|   filename-timestamp order. They tell you what each stage produced and
301|   whether it passed or failed. Failure reports use the `-failure-` infix.
302|   For stages that did NOT opt in, reconstruct from `# Log Entries`, the
303|   session transcript (worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/`
304|   for embedded runs), and the git history.
305|
306|4. **Reconstruct the failure.** For a failed task, check:
307|   - `status: "failed"` in frontmatter.
308|   - The last `# History` entries (e.g. `Stage failed: <reason>`).
309|   - The FAILED stage report (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`; contains
310|     the error and fallback routing).
311|   - `# Log Entries` tail for the actual error output.
312|   - The API's observability `recentFailed` list (if the service is up) for
313|     `failureReason` / `lastError`.
314|
315|5. **Cross-check the deploy** (if the task reached a deploy command — deploys
316|   run as ordinary CI stages now): see `<deploy-state-dir>/history.jsonl`
317|   and `last-result.json` for whether the deploy succeeded and which build
318|   went live.
319|
320|---
321|
322|## 6. Common analysis recipes
323|
324|### "Why did this task fail?"
325|
326|```bash
327|TASK={{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>
328|grep -E "status|currentStageId" "$TASK/task.md"          # where it ended
329|grep -E "^- " "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20                 # last history events
330|grep -rl "FAILED" "$TASK"/*-failure-*.md                  # failed stage reports
331|grep -E "Log Entries" -A 5 "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20    # stored log tail
332|```
333|
334|### "What is running right now?"
335|
336|```bash
337|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
338|```
339|
340|### "Did the last deploy work / what build is live?"
341|
342|```bash
343|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
344|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
345|tail -n 50 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
346|```
347|
348|### "What did the agent actually do in stage X?"
349|
350|Read any stage report `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md` or
351|`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md` (summary, output, modified files) plus
352|the `# Log Entries` section of `task.md`. Agent stages that did not opt into
353|reporting leave no success report — use the session transcript (Runner
354|worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs) and
355|git log.
356|
357|### "Is the service healthy?"
358|
359|```bash
360|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
361|docker compose logs --tail 50 backend          # Docker deployment
362|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 50   # native self-host
363|```
364|
365|---
366|
367|## 7. Gotchas
368|
369|- **Task data is under the project `cwd`, not `{{deployDir}}`.** The deployed
370|  build dir only holds code + `build.json`.
371|- **`task.md` is a snapshot, not a full transcript.** Stored logs are capped
372|  (`KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT`, default 500 entries, oldest evicted under
373|  a marker). For the full agent conversation use the session transcript —
374|  Runner worktree on the Runner host, or the session JSONL in
375|  `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs.
376|- **`.kainbain/` is gitignored** — session transcripts and deploy state are
377|  local-only, not in the repo. Runner worktrees (`kb-<taskId>`) are also
378|  local to the Runner host.
379|- **Absolute backend paths are retargeted on Runners.** The backend curates
380|  prompts with its own project cwd and the Runner rewrites that prefix to
381|  the prepared worktree — a path that exists on the backend may live under
382|  the worktree on the Runner host.
383|- **There is no `deploy` stage type anymore.** Legacy `deploy` (like `script`)
384|  reads as `ci`; merge-plus-deploy composites are migrated into a git-only
385|  merge stage plus a dedicated CI stage. `running_deploy` in old records is a
386|  legacy label.
387|- **`docs/tasks/active/` is human scratch**, not API-written. Don't treat it as
388|  authoritative.
389|- **Auto-generated reports** are marked with
390|  `<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->`; distinguish them from manual ones.
391|- **Agent-stage success reports are opt-in.** A default agent stage that
392|  succeeded leaves NO report file — absence of a `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`
393|  is expected, not data loss. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
394|  are always written.
395|- **The engine is single-threaded** (one global `ExecutionQueue`). Only one
396|  task executes at a time; others queue. `engine.status` is `idle` when nothing
397|  runs.
398|- **Interrupted tasks** (server restart mid-run) are rehydrated with status
399|  `interrupted` and a history entry "Execution recovered after server restart".
400|- **Auto-iteration:** a failed stage may auto re-run (fix → re-test → re-review)
401|  up to `KAINBAIN_MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS` (default 8) before being parked as
402|  `failed`. Each failed attempt leaves a `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`
403|  report; multiple failure files for the same stage = auto-iteration attempts.

6|
7|# KainBain Task Analysis (production)
8|
9|This skill teaches an agent how to investigate **live** and **past** KainBain
10|tasks in a production deployment. It covers the two things you almost always
11|need first: **where the task folder is** and **where the logs are**. Everything
12|else is reading those artifacts.
13|
14|KainBain is an AI task orchestrator. Tasks are created into a project's
15|workflow, advance through stages (`agent`, `human`, `ci`, `merge`), and are
16|persisted as markdown on disk. (Legacy `review` stages read as `human`, and
17|legacy `script` / `deploy` stages read as `ci` — a deploy command is an
18|ordinary CI stage now.) Agent stages run on **Runners**: the backend curates
19|the stage prompt and a Runner executes it in a per-task worktree, syncing
20|task docs/assets in and rewriting the backend cwd prefix to the worktree.
21|The API is Fastify; the frontend is served from the same origin. Production
22|is either Docker Compose (`docker compose up -d`, `https://<app-host>`) or a
23|native self-host where the app runs as a systemd **user** service.
24|
25|---
26|
27|## 1. Example deployment profiles (illustrative, optional)
28|
29|| | Dev | Production |
30|| --- | --- | --- |
31|| Repo / project cwd | `{{projectCwd}}` | same repo, but the *deployed* copy is `{{deployDir}}` |
32|| API base | `{{kbApiBase}}` (or `PORT` env) | the public URL / service `PORT` (override `{{kbApiBase}}` — localhost is dev-only) |
33|| Service | none (run manually) | Docker Compose service, or `<service-unit>` (systemd **user** unit on native self-hosts) |
34|| App URL | `{{kbApiBase}}` | `https://<app-host>` |
35|| Task folders | `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/` | same layout, under the project's `cwd` |
36|| Agent execution | embedded (in-process) | Runner worktree (`kb-<taskId>`, cwd prefix retargeted) |
37|
38|**Key fact:** task folders are written under the **project's `cwd`**, not under
39|`{{deployDir}}`. The project's `cwd` is recorded in
40|`<project cwd>/.kainbain/project.json` (e.g. `"cwd": "{{projectCwd}}"`).
41|Tasks live at:
42|
43|```text
44|{{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>/
45|```
46|
47|`{{deployDir}}` is only the *deployed build* (api + frontend/dist + build.json);
48|it does **not** hold task data. Don't look for tasks there.
49|
50|---
51|
52|## 2. The task folder (the single most important artifact)
53|
54|Every task is a directory under `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/`:
55|
56|```text
57|docs/tasks/<taskId>/
58|├── task.md                      # canonical task entity (frontmatter + body)
59|├── IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md       # plan written by the Plan stage (if used)
60|├── plan-<timestamp>.md          # stage report: Plan (only if the stage opted in)
61|├── <stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md  # failure report (ALWAYS written on stage failure)
62|├── automated-tests-<timestamp>.md # CI / human-checkpoint report (always written)
63|└── ...                          # one report per stage run that produced one
64|```
65|
66|**Reporting is opt-in for agent stages.** A default agent stage writes NO
67|report on success — no agent-authored summary file and no engine-generated
68|one. A stage opts in via `report: true` on the stage config or by attaching
69|the `stage-report` skill. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
70|are always written on stage failure, and CI stages (including legacy
71|`script` / `deploy` commands) and merge stages and human checkpoints always
72|write their own reports.
73|
74|### `task.md` — the canonical record
75|
76|`task.md` is the authoritative, server-written snapshot of the task. Read it
77|first. It has YAML frontmatter and a markdown body:
78|
79|- **Frontmatter:** `id`, `projectId`, `workflowId`, `title`, `status`,
80|  `currentStageId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `enteredStageAt`, `timeInStage`,
81|  `outputReport`, `feedback`, `blockedBy` (plus machine fields such as
82|  `branch`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`).
83|- **`# Goal`** — the task's goal/title.
84|- **`# History`** — an append-only audit trail, one line per event:
85|  `- <ISO timestamp>: <action>` (created, edited, stage advanced, failed, etc.).
86|  This is the fastest way to reconstruct what happened and when.
87|- **`# Timeline`** — one line per stage visit (`<timestamp>: <stage> |
88|  <status> | <duration>`, with a diff stat when the stage touched git).
89|- **`# Log Entries`** — the stored per-task log as structured JSON, capped at
90|  `KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT` entries (default 500, oldest evicted under
91|  a marker). This is the single bound on task log storage. (Very old files may
92|  still carry a rendered `# Process Logs` section instead — legacy files are
93|  parsed back into entries on load.)
94|- `KAINBAIN_PROCESS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (default 32000) only bounds one stage's
95|  captured streamed output kept in memory **while it runs** — it is not the
96|  stored task log.
97|
98|### Stage report files (`<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`, `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
99|
100|Agent-stage success reports are **opt-in** (stage `report: true` or the
101|`stage-report` skill). Failure reports always exist and carry the `-failure-`
102|filename infix. Auto-generated reports carry the marker
103|`<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->` (hidden in most renderers).
104|A report contains: task, stage type, model, duration, status (PASSED/FAILED),
105|summary of changes, execution output, modified files, and verification status.
106|On failure it includes the error and notes the fallback routing.
107|
108|### `docs/tasks/active/`
109|
110|A separate, manually-maintained scratch area (`docs/tasks/active/<taskId>/N.md`)
111|holds working notes per stage. It is **not** written by the API — treat it as
112|human scratch, not authoritative.
113|
114|---
115|
116|## 3. Where the logs live
117|
118|There are **four** distinct log sources. Match the question to the source.
119|
120|### 3a. Service / request logs — container logs or systemd journal
121|
122|The production API logs Fastify structured JSON (`level`, `time`, `pid`,
123|`req`, `res`, `msg`). Where to read it depends on the deployment shape:
124|
125|```bash
126|# Docker Compose deployment
127|docker compose logs -f backend     # tail live service logs
128|docker compose logs --tail 200 backend
129|docker compose ps                  # confirm the service is up
130|
131|# Native self-host (systemd user unit)
132|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -f
133|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -n 200
134|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> --since "2026-10-29 08:00:00"
135|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 100
136|systemctl --user status <service-unit>
137|systemctl --user restart <service-unit>
138|```
139|
140|Use this for: request failures, startup crashes, unhandled errors, and
141|confirming the service is up. On a native self-host the unit file is
142|typically at `~/.config/systemd/user/<service-unit>` (WorkingDirectory
143|`{{deployDir}}/api`, `PORT` set to the API port, `NODE_ENV=production`).
144|
145|### 3b. Deploy logs — `<deploy-state-dir>/`
146|
147|Self-deployment state and logs live under the deploy state directory
148|(typically `~/.kainbain/deploy/` when self-hosting KainBain):
149|
150|```text
151|<deploy-state-dir>/
152|├── deploy.log        # full deploy script output (append-only)
153|├── state.json        # current deploy state
154|├── last-result.json  # last deploy result
155|├── history.jsonl     # append-only deploy history (one JSON per line)
156|├── build.txt         # autoincrementing build counter
157|├── deploy.lock       # flock lock file
158|└── releases/         # per-build release snapshots
159|```
160|
161|The live build number is stamped into `{{deployDir}}/build.json`
162|(`{ buildNumber, deployedAt, commit }`). The header shows `#B<number>` — clicking
163|it opens the KainBain changelog baked into the deploy (`{{deployDir}}/changelog.json`,
164|latest 200 commits on the default branch plus `totalCount`). On Docker
165|deployments the build files live inside the image, not on the host — use the
166|API (`GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/changelog`) instead of host paths.
167|
168|```bash
169|tail -n 200 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
170|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
171|cat <deploy-state-dir>/state.json
172|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
173|```
174|
175|Use this for: "did the deploy succeed / what build is live / why did it roll
176|back". The API also exposes these via `GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/log`,
177|`POST /deploy`, `POST /deploy/rollback`, plus `GET /deploy/changelog` for the
178|baked history (`{ changelog: null, reason: "not-baked" }` before the first
179|deploy that bakes it).
180|
181|### 3c. Agent session transcripts — worktree (Runner) or `.kainbain/sessions/` (embedded)
182|
183|Runner-executed stages keep their session where the harness ran: the
184|per-task worktree on the **Runner host** (`sessionDir` = the worktree), not on
185|the backend. Only embedded (non-Runner) runs write transcripts to the
186|backend's `<project cwd>/.kainbain/sessions/` — one JSONL transcript per
187|session (one JSON object per line): `session`, `model_change`,
188|`thinking_level_change`, and message/tool events, resumed via the SDK's
189|`SessionManager`.
190|
191|```bash
192|ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/
193|head -5 {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/*.jsonl
194|```
195|
196|Use this for: the raw agent conversation / model used / thinking level for a
197|project. Always check **which host ran the stage** first — for Runner tasks
198|the transcript is on the Runner host, and the backend directory may not have
199|it. Note: `.kainbain/` is gitignored, so these are local-only.
200|
201|### 3d. Per-task logs — `# Log Entries` in `task.md`, Live Console on the wire
202|
203|The stored agent/tool/CI output for a task is the `# Log Entries` section of
204|`task.md` (see §2). Live output streams over the WebSocket as `PROCESS_STDOUT`
205|/ `process:stdout` frames, which is what the UI's Live Console renders — for a
206|running task, watch the socket (see §4b), not the file. `task.md` is
207|rewritten on every state change, so its frontmatter, `# History`, and
208|`# Log Entries` stay current, but there is no rendered process-log tail to
209|`tail -f` anymore.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 4. Analysing a **live** task
214|
215|A "live" task is one currently executing or queued. The engine is a single
216|global executor (`ExecutionQueue`) with an `engineState` snapshot.
217|
218|### 4a. Via the API (fastest, no filesystem)
219|
220|```bash
221|# Engine state: what is running right now
222|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
223|
224|# Full observability: engine + health + build + task metrics
225|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
226|
227|# Health
228|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
229|
230|# List tasks for a project (projectId optional → active project)
231|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
232|
233|# Single task (full state incl. history, reports, log entries)
234|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/<taskId>?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
235|
236|# Task queue
237|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/queue?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
238|
239|# Session status (active, streaming, message count, disk session)
240|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/session/status?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
241|```
242|
243|`GET /status/observability` returns `engine` (status, activeTaskId,
244|activeStageId, activeStageName, activeStageType), `build`, `health`, and
245|`observability` (totals: completed/failed/running/waitingHuman/paused/blocked,
246|plus recent completed/failed lists with failure reasons).
247|
248|### 4b. Via WebSocket (live streaming)
249|
250|The frontend subscribes to `GET /ws?projectId=<projectId>` (WebSocket upgrade).
251|Events are JSON `{ type, sessionId, payload, timestamp }`. Key types:
252|`CONNECTED`, `ENGINE_STATE`, `TASK_UPDATED`, `TASK_DELETED`, `NOTIFICATION`,
253|`PROCESS_STDOUT` / `process:stdout`, and agent events (`agent_start`,
254|`tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`,
255|`message_update`, `error`). The UI's **Live Console** (Observability dashboard)
256|renders these with severity tags (`AGENT`, `CI`, `ERROR`, `HUMAN`, `TOOL`).
257|
258|To watch live from a script, connect to the WebSocket endpoint at
259|`{{kbApiBase}}/ws?projectId=<id>` (upgrade `http`→`ws` / `https`→`wss`) and log
260|incoming frames.
261|
262|### 4c. Via the filesystem
263|
264|For a live task, `task.md` is rewritten on every state change, so
265|`tail -f docs/tasks/<taskId>/task.md` shows frontmatter, `# History`, and
266|`# Log Entries` growing in near-real-time (watch the WebSocket for the
267|live stream itself — see §3d). The `status` frontmatter tells you where it
268|is: `running_agent`, `running_ci`, `running_merge`, `advancing`, `in_stage`,
269|`waiting_human`, `paused`, `failed`, `completed` (`interrupted` after an
270|unclean restart; `running_deploy` is a legacy label from before the deploy
271|runtime was removed). Note: with Runner execution, absolute backend-cwd paths
272|in prompts are retargeted to the task worktree — resolve worktree-relative
273|paths against `kb-<taskId>`, not the backend checkout.
274|
275|---

374|  Runner worktree on the Runner host, or the session JSONL in
375|  `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs.
376|- **`.kainbain/` is gitignored** — session transcripts and deploy state are
377|  local-only, not in the repo. Runner worktrees (`kb-<taskId>`) are also
378|  local to the Runner host.
379|- **Absolute backend paths are retargeted on Runners.** The backend curates
380|  prompts with its own project cwd and the Runner rewrites that prefix to
381|  the prepared worktree — a path that exists on the backend may live under
382|  the worktree on the Runner host.
383|- **There is no `deploy` stage type anymore.** Legacy `deploy` (like `script`)
384|  reads as `ci`; merge-plus-deploy composites are migrated into a git-only
385|  merge stage plus a dedicated CI stage. `running_deploy` in old records is a
386|  legacy label.
387|- **`docs/tasks/active/` is human scratch**, not API-written. Don't treat it as
388|  authoritative.
389|- **Auto-generated reports** are marked with
390|  `<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->`; distinguish them from manual ones.
391|- **Agent-stage success reports are opt-in.** A default agent stage that
392|  succeeded leaves NO report file — absence of a `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`
393|  is expected, not data loss. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
394|  are always written.
395|- **The engine is single-threaded** (one global `ExecutionQueue`). Only one
396|  task executes at a time; others queue. `engine.status` is `idle` when nothing
397|  runs.
398|- **Interrupted tasks** (server restart mid-run) are rehydrated with status
399|  `interrupted` and a history entry "Execution recovered after server restart".
400|- **Auto-iteration:** a failed stage may auto re-run (fix → re-test → re-review)
401|  up to `KAINBAIN_MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS` (default 8) before being parked as
402|  `failed`. Each failed attempt leaves a `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`
403|  report; multiple failure files for the same stage = auto-iteration attempts.

## S1 — Cap refusals must not count as runner deaths; add re-dispatch backoff (backend-only)

**Answers Cause 1 + part of the amplifier.** All 49 reasoned interrupts are
`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals, yet `interruptExecution` increments
`runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally, so five capacity refusals park the task as a
`runner-death-loop` (42 escalations fleet-wide). And every interrupt re-dispatches
in ~150 ms with Rule-0 priority, so the same still-full runner re-claims instantly.

**Proposed change (backend, `api/`):**
1. In `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution`: do not increment
   `runnerInterruptCount` (and do not escalate) when the reason indicates graceful
   capacity refusal — i.e. reason starts with `Runner workdir unavailable:`.
   Record the refusal in history as today (keep the reason string; it is the
   detector), but track it on a separate counter (e.g. `capacityRefusalCount`)
   with its own operator-visibility threshold rather than the death bound.
2. In the scheduler (`api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js` / `findResumedCandidate.js`):
   add backoff for repeatedly resumed tasks — e.g. after N consecutive resumes of the
   same task+stage, delay re-dispatch (bootstrapped small, e.g. 30 s → 5 min) and/or
   sort behind fresh work, and prefer dispatch to a *different* runner than the one
   that just refused. Keep the first resume fast (today's behaviour) so genuine
   one-off flakes still recover instantly.
3. Keep `isAutoResumableWithReason.js` `runner-death-loop` parking for true death
   streaks (crashes with no capacity reason).

**Tests (from `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` / GUIDE-01 + GUIDE-07):**
- Red: `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` — five cap-reason
  interrupts leave `runnerInterruptCount` at 0, no `runner-death-loop` park.
- Red: `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` — after N
  consecutive resumes, fresh work wins over the flapping task.
- Keep a pin: five *bare/crash* interrupts still park (existing behaviour in
  `executionLedger.test.js` around line 778 must keep passing).

**How to confirm the bug (before writing the fix):**
- Local (SAFE-LOCAL): run the GUIDE-01 §3 backend snippet — it demonstrates five
  cap refusals parking as `runner-death-loop` on current code.
- Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): `GET /tasks/<id>` on `350ca162`,
  `db24c124`, `7b69d365` — confirm cap-reason strings followed by `Runner deaths
  escalated` at count 5. After the fix + deploy (backend-only, no runner rollout):
  re-run the same histories on new interrupts and the GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script —
  `escalated` should drop while `with_reason` stays visible.

**Parallel/blocking:** none. Backend-only; safe to ship first.
**Risk:** low-medium. Touching the escalation rule changes parking behaviour — the
pin tests above are the guard. Smallest safe slice is the counter exclusion alone;
backoff can be a second commit in the same task if review prefers.

## S2 — Fix the 413 completion-payload loop (backend limit + runner payload + no crash on 413)

**Answers Cause 2 (proven: 5 crash-loop laps on `7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 11-20
21:19–21:47, restart counters 830→834).** After a fully successful run + push, the
`complete-execution` POST exceeds Fastify's default 1 MiB JSON body limit
(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`) and is rejected with 413; the daemon's
generic catch interrupts (bare on 0.1.0) and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart →
full stage re-run → same 413. Deterministic, burns a whole run per lap.

**Proposed change (both sides; either half alone breaks the loop, both together
remove the class):**
1. Backend: set an explicit `bodyLimit` for the runner `complete-execution` route
   (raise to a deliberate value, e.g. 10 MiB — document why, do not just copy the
   accessibility route's value without checking it) and log rejected oversize
   bodies with task id + byte size so the next 413 is diagnosable from backend
   logs instead of invisible (today the backend rejects before routing and leaves
   no task-history trace).
2. Runner: shrink `collectTaskFiles` (`runner/daemon.js:1820`) so the envelope
   cannot exceed the agreed limit — exclude binary assets (PNG screenshots) or
   downsample the file set, and account for `output` (20 KiB) + JSON overhead in
   the cumulative cap rather than capping the files array at 1 MiB and then adding
   the envelope on top.
3. Runner: treat HTTP 413 from `complete-execution` as a deterministic,
   non-retryable completion failure (report once as failed with the size details,
   return — never rethrow). A 413 is proof the stage ran fine and only the report
   was too big; it must never become an interrupt + restart.

- `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` (GUIDE-02 §3) — many sub-256 KiB files +

- Daemon-level: stubbed `client.complete` throwing a 413-shaped error → failed
  completion recorded, no interrupt, no rethrow (mirror the GUIDE-04 §3 shape).

**How to confirm the bug:**
- Local (SAFE-LOCAL): the GUIDE-02 §2 `app.inject` test proves >1 MiB bodies get

- Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): backend access log 11-20 21:15–21:47 for

**Parallel/blocking:** none on other solutions. Internal order: backend limit raise
can ship before the runner payload shrink (backend deploys immediately; runner needs
rollout). Coordinate the agreed limit value between the two halves in the task's plan.
**Risk:** low. Raising a body limit is safe; the runner shrink must keep task-docs

## S6 — Fix the misleading display: resume label + "Tried N times" (backend + frontend)

**Answers the amplifier's display half — the cheapest, lowest-risk task, and the one
that fixes what the reporter actually saw.** `autoResumeTask` uses one history string
for both recovery routes, so 100 runner-path resumes display as "server restarts that
never happened" (0 recorded); `summarizeStageRuns` counts every `Resumed` row into
`tryCount`, producing the screenshot's ×6/×10/×11 badges.

**Proposed change:**
1. Backend (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`): distinct history strings per
   recovery route — keep `Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue`
   for genuine reconcile recoveries, add e.g. `Auto-resumed after runner interrupt —
   prioritised in queue` (include runner id + reason when present) for runner-path
   resumes. Use the existing `interruptedBy` marker to pick the route.
2. Frontend (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js` `summarizeStageRuns`,
   `:483-536`): exclude `Resumed` rows from `tryCount` (they are infra re-tries, not
   stage attempts) — or show them separately (e.g. `Tried 2 times · 4 infra resumes`).
   Update `formatTryCount` (`:556`) accordingly.
3. Update the existing pins that encode current behaviour (`taskFormatters.test.js`
   `summarizeStageRuns` cases, `taskScheduler.test.js:896` autoResume block,
   `stallRecovery`/`startupRecovery` integration tests referencing the label) —
   this is an intended contract change, not a regression; each updated assertion must
   state the new expected string/count explicitly.

counted into badges, runner-path resumes labelled "server restart".
**Parallel/blocking:** fully independent. Good first task.
**Risk:** low. User-visible strings change — keep old-row rendering backward compatible
(histories already written keep the old string; only new resumes use the new one).

## S7 — Regression-pin the boot reconcile + keep Cause 6 ruled out (tiny backend test task)

**Cause 6 is ruled out (0/118, publish-only deploys, observed restart orphaned

2|
3|Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
4|Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: triage of `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` + replication guides into
5|reviewable, parallelisable follow-up tasks.

9|`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, and `assets/image.png` (task `7f6220c3` timeline showing repeated

17|
