64|## S1 — Cap refusals must not count as runner deaths; add re-dispatch backoff (backend-only)
65|
66|**Answers Cause 1 + part of the amplifier.** All 49 reasoned interrupts are
67|`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals, yet `interruptExecution` increments
68|`runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally, so five capacity refusals park the task as a
69|`runner-death-loop` (42 escalations fleet-wide). And every interrupt re-dispatches
70|in ~150 ms with Rule-0 priority, so the same still-full runner re-claims instantly.
71|
72|**Proposed change (backend, `api/`):**
73|1. In `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution`: do not increment
74|   `runnerInterruptCount` (and do not escalate) when the reason indicates graceful
75|   capacity refusal — i.e. reason starts with `Runner workdir unavailable:`.
76|   Record the refusal in history as today (keep the reason string; it is the
77|   detector), but track it on a separate counter (e.g. `capacityRefusalCount`)
78|   with its own operator-visibility threshold rather than the death bound.
79|2. In the scheduler (`api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js` / `findResumedCandidate.js`):
80|   add backoff for repeatedly resumed tasks — e.g. after N consecutive resumes of the
81|   same task+stage, delay re-dispatch (bootstrapped small, e.g. 30 s → 5 min) and/or
82|   sort behind fresh work, and prefer dispatch to a *different* runner than the one
83|   that just refused. Keep the first resume fast (today's behaviour) so genuine
84|   one-off flakes still recover instantly.
85|3. Keep `isAutoResumableWithReason.js` `runner-death-loop` parking for true death
86|   streaks (crashes with no capacity reason).
87|
88|**Tests (from `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` / GUIDE-01 + GUIDE-07):**
89|- Red: `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js` — five cap-reason
90|  interrupts leave `runnerInterruptCount` at 0, no `runner-death-loop` park.
91|- Red: `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` — after N
92|  consecutive resumes, fresh work wins over the flapping task.
93|- Keep a pin: five *bare/crash* interrupts still park (existing behaviour in
94|  `executionLedger.test.js` around line 778 must keep passing).
95|
96|**How to confirm the bug (before writing the fix):**
97|- Local (SAFE-LOCAL): run the GUIDE-01 §3 backend snippet — it demonstrates five
98|  cap refusals parking as `runner-death-loop` on current code.
99|- Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): `GET /tasks/<id>` on `350ca162`,
100|  `db24c124`, `7b69d365` — confirm cap-reason strings followed by `Runner deaths
101|  escalated` at count 5. After the fix + deploy (backend-only, no runner rollout):
102|  re-run the same histories on new interrupts and the GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script —
103|  `escalated` should drop while `with_reason` stays visible.
104|
105|**Parallel/blocking:** none. Backend-only; safe to ship first.
106|**Risk:** low-medium. Touching the escalation rule changes parking behaviour — the
107|pin tests above are the guard. Smallest safe slice is the counter exclusion alone;
108|backoff can be a second commit in the same task if review prefers.
109|
110|## S2 — Fix the 413 completion-payload loop (backend limit + runner payload + no crash on 413)
111|
112|**Answers Cause 2 (proven: 5 crash-loop laps on `7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 11-20
113|21:19–21:47, restart counters 830→834).** After a fully successful run + push, the
114|`complete-execution` POST exceeds Fastify's default 1 MiB JSON body limit
115|(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`) and is rejected with 413; the daemon's
116|generic catch interrupts (bare on 0.1.0) and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart →
117|full stage re-run → same 413. Deterministic, burns a whole run per lap.
118|
119|**Proposed change (both sides; either half alone breaks the loop, both together
120|remove the class):**
121|1. Backend: set an explicit `bodyLimit` for the runner `complete-execution` route
122|   (raise to a deliberate value, e.g. 10 MiB — document why, do not just copy the
123|   accessibility route's value without checking it) and log rejected oversize
124|   bodies with task id + byte size so the next 413 is diagnosable from backend
125|   logs instead of invisible (today the backend rejects before routing and leaves
126|   no task-history trace).
127|2. Runner: shrink `collectTaskFiles` (`runner/daemon.js:1820`) so the envelope
128|   cannot exceed the agreed limit — exclude binary assets (PNG screenshots) or
129|   downsample the file set, and account for `output` (20 KiB) + JSON overhead in
130|   the cumulative cap rather than capping the files array at 1 MiB and then adding
131|   the envelope on top.
132|3. Runner: treat HTTP 413 from `complete-execution` as a deterministic,
133|   non-retryable completion failure (report once as failed with the size details,
134|   return — never rethrow). A 413 is proof the stage ran fine and only the report
135|   was too big; it must never become an interrupt + restart.
136|
137|**Tests:**
138|- Pin (passes today): `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` + `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js`
139|  (GUIDE-02 §2) — then flip to assert the new explicit limit after the change.
140|- `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` (GUIDE-02 §3) — many sub-256 KiB files +
141|  output + envelope must stay under the agreed limit.
142|- Daemon-level: stubbed `client.complete` throwing a 413-shaped error → failed
143|  completion recorded, no interrupt, no rethrow (mirror the GUIDE-04 §3 shape).
144|
145|**How to confirm the bug:**
146|- Local (SAFE-LOCAL): the GUIDE-02 §2 `app.inject` test proves >1 MiB bodies get
147|  413 on current wiring; the §3 test proves the file+envelope composition exceeds it.
148|- Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): backend access log 11-20 21:15–21:47 for
149|  the five 413s + sizes (E2); `Backend 413` sweep on both runner journals (E3);
150|  `kb-7f6220c3` worktree shows pushed stage-output commits for the looped executions
151|  (do NOT reap that worktree — it is the exhibit). After fix: no new `Backend 413`
152|  lines; any future oversize report surfaces as a failed completion with size details.
153|
154|**Parallel/blocking:** none on other solutions. Internal order: backend limit raise
155|can ship before the runner payload shrink (backend deploys immediately; runner needs
156|rollout). Coordinate the agreed limit value between the two halves in the task's plan.
157|**Risk:** low. Raising a body limit is safe; the runner shrink must keep task-docs
158|sync useful (assert the kept-file set in tests).
159|
160|## S3 — Investigate the local-alpha setup-phase deaths (evidence task, then targeted fix)
161|
162|**Answers Cause 3 — the volume-dominant signature (96/118 local-alpha, 99/118 ≤15 s
163|after `started`, median 4.7 s, no `prompted`).** The fault is localised to
164|`prepareWorkdir` but genuinely unnamed, because deployed 0.1.0 attaches no reason on
165|the generic path. Writing a fix now would be guessing.
166|
167|**Proposed task shape — strict two-phase, investigation first:**
168|1. Phase A (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs explicit permission + backend-host access):
169|   collect E1 — local-alpha daemon journal on `192.168.1.206` (user `server`) for
170|   the exhibit windows (`c5c465c4` 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` 11-20 15:38–15:43,
171|   18:39–18:41, 11-21 10:16 + 13:34): the `Runner failed: <message>` lines name the
172|   fault, restart-counter deltas separate crash-loops from in-process re-claim loops.
173|   Also E6: runner build provenance via `GET /runners`, plus work-root/disk/git-mirror
174|   health on the backend host at those times. Exact commands are in GUIDE-03 §4.
175|2. Phase B: write the targeted fix from whatever Phase A names (likely candidates:
176|   git lock/fetch/push-race handling, docs-worktree handling — note `7f6220c3` IS the
177|   separate-docs-repo task — stale mirror, disk/permissions). If Phase A is
178|   inconclusive, the fallback deliverable is defined hardening, not a shrug:
179|   per-step timing + error capture inside `prepareWorkdir` so the next occurrence
180|   self-diagnoses, plus the generic S4 containment below.
181|3. Cheap parallel hardening that does NOT wait for Phase A (include in this task or
182|   S4, reviewer's call): assert/record the runner version on every interrupt history
183|   row so old-build bare interrupts stay attributable (GUIDE-03 §2 TDD angle).
184|
185|**Tests:** GUIDE-03 §2 backend storm pin + `runner/project.setupFaults.test.js`
186|failure-shape pins (§3) are the regression floor. The Phase-B fix must add its own
187|red test reproducing the named fault in a temp work root.
188|**How to confirm the bug:** Phase A *is* the confirmation — a `Runner failed:`
189|message timestamp-joined to a `started` → bare-interrupt pair. Post-0.2.x-rollout
190|(S5), bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should name this cause directly;
191|re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
192|**Parallel/blocking:** Phase A is independent and can start immediately (needs access
193|permission, not code). Phase B (S3b) is the only task in this response blocked on
194|another task's output. Prod *confirmation* of the fix waits on the S5 rollout.
195|**Risk:** low (read-only) for Phase A. Do not let Phase B expand into "rewrite
196|setup" — one named fault, one fix, one red test.
197|
198|## S4 — Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal (daemon containment)
199|
200|**Answers Cause 4 (501 `fetch failed` + 16 `Backend 502` since 11-19 on server2-alpha;
201|a proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).** Today any
202|in-`try` backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and
203|rethrows → process exit → systemd restart. Heartbeat failures are tolerated (lease
204|TTL) but in-assignment call failures are fatal, so every LAN blip or backend restart
205|window can kill a run.
206|
207|**Proposed change (runner, `runner/daemon.js` + `runner/client.js`):**
208|1. In the `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2452`): transient backend
209|   errors (`fetch failed` network errors, 502/503/504 status) during an assignment
210|   send an interrupt *with reason* and **return** (keep polling) instead of rethrowing —
211|   the same report-and-return precedent as the existing `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and
212|   deterministic-`gitFailure` branches. Lease TTL already bounds the damage.
213|2. Add bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (heartbeat, dispatch poll)
214|   so the idle loop stops crash-cycling (restart counters 366→367 in the 11-19 sample)
215|   — or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit on those paths.
216|3. Keep fatal: `STALE_EPOCH` (epoch fencing must propagate), auth failures, and
217|   genuinely unknown errors — enumerate the non-fatal set explicitly (status codes +
218|   `fetch failed` cause) rather than inverting the catch-all, so new failure modes
219|   stay loud.
220|
221|**Must-read before coding:** `docs/tasks/db49d6c6-*/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`
222|(runner recovery containment) — build on it or scope against it; do not land a
223|second competing catch-restructure.
224|**Tests:** `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (GUIDE-04 §2: 502 shape, dropped-socket
225|shape, recovery) + the §3 daemon fatality-boundary test flipped red
226|(`expect(rethrown).toBe(false)` for transient errors, still-true for stale-epoch).
227|Register any new `runner/*.test.js` in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (`buildBranches`).
228|**How to confirm the bug:** local — the §2/§3 tests fail-or-pin the fatality on current
229|code. Prod (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission): E4 timestamp-join of server2-alpha
230|`Runner failed: fetch failed|Backend 502` lines against `started` → interrupt pairs
231|on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`; E7 backend/proxy
232|availability log for 11-19 → 11-21. After rollout: crash-restart rate in the runner
233|journal drops while assignment success rate holds.
234|**Parallel/blocking:** code-independent of S1/S2/S6. Shares the daemon catch with the
235|`db49d6c6` work — sequence with that task, not with anything here.
236|**Risk:** medium. Changing fatal→non-fatal can mask real failures — the explicit
237|non-fatal enumeration + reason-on-interrupt + journal loudness are the guards.
238|
239|## S5 — Roll out 0.2.x runners and run the fleet before/after recount (ops + verification)
240|
241|**Covers Cause 5 verification and unlocks diagnosis of Causes 3–4.** Deployed runners
242|are 0.1.0 (main `f430f53`, 11-11); repo is 0.2.0 with interrupt reasons and
243|deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`).
244|Rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle-converge
245|(`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so lag is expected — but until it lands, every new
246|interrupt is still bare and every commit-hook rejection still crash-loops.
247|
248|**Proposed steps:**
249|1. Confirm both runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge to the build
250|   containing `046a6391` per the runbook; record `GET /runners` versions before/after.
251|2. Re-run the `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2` counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script: bare
252|   interrupts should drop to ~0, reasons should name Causes 1/3/4 directly, and
253|   deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED completions with
254|   `gitFailure` payloads, never as interrupts.
255|3. Run the E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4): for each remaining post-`finished`
256|   interrupt, check `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`,
257|   `7f6220c3`) for stage-output-commit presence (present → Cause 2/4 territory;
258|   absent → Cause 5). Only if E5 finds commit-loop cases the `046a6391` fix does not
259|   cover should a new Cause-5 code task be created.
260|4. Record the post-rollout counts in the task folder as the new baseline for S1–S4.
261|
262|**How to confirm the underlying bugs:** this task *is* the confirmation harness —
263|before/after counts plus the journal sweeps (E3 `Backend 413`, E4 502/fetch-fail,
264|E5 hook/commit lines). No new unit tests; deliverable is the recount + version record.
265|**Parallel/blocking:** runs in parallel with all code work; only prod *confirmation*
266|of S3/S4/S2-runner-half waits on it.
267|**Risk:** low. Follow the runbook; do not force-restart runners mid-assignment to
268|speed convergence (observe only — forced restarts are PROD-ACTION and risk new
269|interrupts, which is exactly what we are measuring).
270|
271|## S6 — Fix the misleading display: resume label + "Tried N times" (backend + frontend)
272|
273|**Answers the amplifier's display half — the cheapest, lowest-risk task, and the one
274|that fixes what the reporter actually saw.** `autoResumeTask` uses one history string
275|for both recovery routes, so 100 runner-path resumes display as "server restarts that
276|never happened" (0 recorded); `summarizeStageRuns` counts every `Resumed` row into
277|`tryCount`, producing the screenshot's ×6/×10/×11 badges.
278|
279|**Proposed change:**
280|1. Backend (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`): distinct history strings per
281|   recovery route — keep `Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue`
282|   for genuine reconcile recoveries, add e.g. `Auto-resumed after runner interrupt —
283|   prioritised in queue` (include runner id + reason when present) for runner-path
284|   resumes. Use the existing `interruptedBy` marker to pick the route.
285|2. Frontend (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js` `summarizeStageRuns`,
286|   `:483-536`): exclude `Resumed` rows from `tryCount` (they are infra re-tries, not
287|   stage attempts) — or show them separately (e.g. `Tried 2 times · 4 infra resumes`).
288|   Update `formatTryCount` (`:556`) accordingly.
289|3. Update the existing pins that encode current behaviour (`taskFormatters.test.js`
290|   `summarizeStageRuns` cases, `taskScheduler.test.js:896` autoResume block,
291|   `stallRecovery`/`startupRecovery` integration tests referencing the label) —
292|   this is an intended contract change, not a regression; each updated assertion must
293|   state the new expected string/count explicitly.
294|
295|**Tests:** `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` (GUIDE-07 §2 — pin-then-red),
296|frontend `summarizeStageRuns` pin-then-red (§4). Full gate: `npm run test:api`,
297|`npm run test:frontend`.
298|**How to confirm the bug:** local — the §2/§4 pin tests pass on current code, proving
299|the mislabel and the inflation; the red tests fail until fixed. Prod (read-only):
300|map `assets/image.png`-style rows to `GET /tasks/7f6220c3` history — Resumed rows
301|counted into badges, runner-path resumes labelled "server restart".
302|**Parallel/blocking:** fully independent. Good first task.
303|**Risk:** low. User-visible strings change — keep old-row rendering backward compatible
304|(histories already written keep the old string; only new resumes use the new one).

306|## S7 — Regression-pin the boot reconcile + keep Cause 6 ruled out (tiny backend test task)
307|
308|**Cause 6 is ruled out (0/118, publish-only deploys, observed restart orphaned
309|nothing) — this task keeps it ruled out.** `reconcileInterruptedRuns` is the one path
310|that *should* write `interrupted by server restart`; pin it so future boot-order or
311|status-set changes are caught, and re-run the zero-count check after each deploy.
312|
313|**Proposed change:** add `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js`
314|exactly as specified in GUIDE-06 §2 (orphan flip + history row, engine-owned task

{
  "round": 1,
  "generatedAt": "2026-11-21T14:07:53.000Z",

  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "Today, when a runner is full, each refused task counts as a runner death, and 5 in a row parks the task as a 'runner-death-loop' (42 tasks parked fleet-wide). We plan to stop counting 'runner full' refusals as deaths, so they never park a task this way (they will still be recorded, with a separate counter for operators). Are you happy with that?",
      "options": [
        "Yes - 'runner full' refusals should never park a task (Recommended)",
        "Yes, but still park after a much higher number of refusals",
        "No - keep parking after 5 like today"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "Today, an interrupted task is re-queued instantly with top priority, so a task can flap on the same full runner within milliseconds. We plan to keep the first retry instant, but slow down repeats (roughly 30 seconds growing to 5 minutes), let fresh work jump ahead, and prefer sending the retry to a different runner. Are you happy with that?",
      "options": [
        "Yes - slow down repeat retries and let fresh work go first (Recommended)",
        "Yes, but only add the delay - keep retry priority unchanged",
        "No - keep instant top-priority retries for all"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q3",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "Some completion reports are too big to send (over the 1 MB limit), which rejects them and re-runs the whole stage in a loop. To shrink reports, the runner would stop sending screenshots/binary files (or send fewer files), so task docs may contain fewer attachments. We would also raise the size limit (e.g. to 10 MB). Are you happy with that?",
      "options": [
        "Yes - exclude screenshots/binary files and raise the limit (Recommended)",
        "Yes - shrink reports some other way but keep screenshots (describe in Notes)",
        "No - keep sending all files even if reports stay large"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q4",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "If a completion report is still too big after the shrink above, what should happen? (Today it loops: interrupt, restart the runner, re-run the whole stage, fail again. We plan to mark the task as failed once, with the size details, and never loop.)",
      "options": [
        "Yes - mark it failed once with size details, never loop (Recommended)",
        "No - keep retrying the stage"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q5",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "Today, any backend hiccup mid-task (network blip, backend restart showing as 502/503/504) crashes the whole runner and restarts it. We plan to make only those transient backend errors non-fatal: the affected task is still interrupted with a reason, but the runner stays alive and keeps working. Anything else (login/auth failures, stale-epoch fencing, unknown errors) still crashes/restarts loudly. Are you happy with that?",
      "options": [
        "Yes - survive network/502/503/504 blips, keep everything else fatal (Recommended)",
        "Make more error types non-fatal too (describe in Notes)",
        "No - keep crashing/restarting the runner on backend errors"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q6",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "Today, every auto-resume in task history says 'Auto-resumed after server restart', even when it was a runner interruption (100 runner-path resumes, 0 real server restarts). We plan to use two labels going forward: keep the server-restart label for genuine restarts, and add an 'Auto-resumed after runner interrupt' label with runner and reason. Old rows stay as they are. Are you happy with that?",
      "options": [
        "Yes - use separate labels for server restarts vs runner interrupts (Recommended)",
        "No - keep the single 'server restart' label"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q7",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "Today, the 'Tried N times' badge counts every infrastructure resume, inflating it (e.g. x6/x10/x11 in the screenshot). We plan to stop counting infra resumes as tries, so badge numbers will go down. Which display do you prefer?",
      "options": [
        "Show infra resumes separately, e.g. 'Tried 2 times, 4 infra resumes' (Recommended)",
        "Just exclude infra resumes (show 'Tried 2 times')",
        "No - keep counting every resume in 'Tried N times'"
      ],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q8",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "The biggest group of interruptions (fast local-alpha deaths a few seconds after start) has no named cause yet, so the fix cannot be written blind. We plan a read-only investigation first: reading the local-alpha runner journal and backend-host health around the known incident windows. Do you approve that prod read-only access?",
      "options": [
        "Yes - allow read-only prod journal/log access for the investigation (Recommended)",
        "No - investigate without any prod access"

      "options": [
        "Yes - gradual rollout, never force-restart mid-task (Recommended)",
        "Yes - roll out faster even if it interrupts running tasks",
        "No - hold the rollout for now"
      ],

275|for both recovery routes, so 100 runner-path resumes display as "server restarts that
276|never happened" (0 recorded); `summarizeStageRuns` counts every `Resumed` row into
277|`tryCount`, producing the screenshot's ×6/×10/×11 badges.

1|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — high level of task interruptions
2|
3|Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
4|Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: DO research (investigatory only — no solutions proposed).
5|
6|## 0. Inputs
7|
8|- **Bug report**: many tasks end with interruptions suggesting flakiness; reporter
9|  notes a `local-alpha` runner restart-loop incident and wonders if it is related;
10|  interruptions "should happen rarely but they are seemingly quite common".
11|- **Screenshot** (`assets/image.png`): task `7f6220c3` ("add support for projects
12|  having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo") showing repeated
13|  "Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and high
14|  "Tried N times" counts (Merge resolver ×6, Quick review ×6, Automated
15|  tests ×10, In Progress ×11).
16|- **Survey result**: the Questionnaire stage recorded `Survey completed (none)` —
17|  the `question-me` skill requested no survey questions, so there is no
18|  `SURVEY.md` with human answers. All evidence below comes from repo code,
19|  the live backend API, runner worktrees, and the runner systemd journal.
20|
21|## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)
22|
23|Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):
24|
25|1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
26|   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
27|   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
28|   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
29|   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
30|   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
31|2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
32|   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
33|   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
34|   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
35|   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
36|   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
37|   an authenticated runner daemon.
38|
39|Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
40|`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
41|`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
42|server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
43|function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
44|`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
45|same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
46|(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
47|(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).
48|
49|## 2. Fleet-wide numbers (live backend, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21)
50|
51|| Signal | Count | Notes |
52||---|---|---|
53|| Runner-path interrupts (`interrupted execution`) | 118 | across 30/61 tasks (~half the project) |
54|| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
55|| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
56|| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
57|| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
58|| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
59|| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
60|| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
61|| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
62|| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |
63|
64|Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
65|(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
66|`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
67|try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
68|localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
69|Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
70|`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.
71|
72|Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
73|`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
74|worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
75|and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
76|`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle
77|converge (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so rollout lag is expected.
78|
79|## 3. Possible causes
80|
81|### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)
82|
83|**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
84|workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
85|reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
86|Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
87|runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
88|the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
89|suspected death loop.
90|
91|**Pros (for).**
92|- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)
93|  carry `Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5); ...
94|  (every orphan was used recently, nothing stale to evict)`. Both hosts appear
95|  (`/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` = local-alpha host, `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` =
96|  server2-alpha host).
97|- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
98|  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
99|- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
100|  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
101|- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
102|  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
103|  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.
104|
105|**Cons (against).**
106|- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
107|  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
108|  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
109|  both hosts).
110|- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
111|- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike
112|  (48 bare) needs a different driver.
113|
114|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
115|- `350ca162` (12 cap interrupts), `db24c124` (9), `7b69d365` (6), `3c12ffcd`
116|  (5), `f56e9878` (4), `1f8959ca` (5) — confirm each shows the cap reason and
117|  same-runner re-claim.
118|- Runner-side: work-root occupancy time series per host around 11-09 and
119|  11-16/17; orphan-staleness / LRU-eviction decisions in daemon logs.
120|- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
(more lines below)

21|## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)
22|
23|Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):
24|

28|   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
29|   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
30|   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
31|2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
32|   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
33|   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
34|   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
35|   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
36|   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
37|   an authenticated runner daemon.
38|
39|Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
40|`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
41|`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
42|server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
43|function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
44|`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
45|same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
46|(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
47|(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).
48|

50|
51|| Signal | Count | Notes |

53|| Runner-path interrupts (`interrupted execution`) | 118 | across 30/61 tasks (~half the project) |
54|| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
55|| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
56|| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
57|| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
58|| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
59|| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
60|| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
61|| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
62|| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |
63|
64|Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
65|(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
66|`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
67|try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
68|localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
69|Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
70|`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.
71|
72|Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
73|`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
74|worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
75|and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
76|`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle
77|converge (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so rollout lag is expected.

100|  re-claim cycles without process restarts.

102|  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
103|  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

107|  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap

109|  both hosts).

(119 line(s) above)
120|- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
121|  cheapest ongoing detector (no host access needed).
122|
123|### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)
124|
125|**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
126|(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
127|backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
128|(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
129|a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
130|agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
131|each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
132|run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
133|(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
134|up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
135|top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
136|output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
137|(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`; the only explicit `bodyLimit` in the
138|API is the accessibility route).
139|
140|**Pros (for).**
141|- Smoking gun in the server2-alpha journal (`journalctl --user
142|  -u kainbain-runner-server2-alpha`): on 11-20, five consecutive cycles of
143|  `Committed <sha> (pushed: true)` → `Runner failed: Backend 413 on
144|  /tasks/7f6220c3-.../complete-execution` → `Main process exited, status=1`
145|  → `Scheduled restart job, restart counter 830→834`, at 21:19, 21:29, 21:35,
146|  21:43, 21:47 — exactly matching the five `finished` → bare-interrupt pairs
147|  in task `7f6220c3` history.
148|- Worktree forensics agree: `kb-7f6220c3` holds the pushed stage-output commits
149|  with matching timestamps, and `origin` has them — proving failure happened
150|  strictly after push.
151|- Deterministic: same task files every lap → same 413 → loop only ends via the
152|  death-bound park (observed: parked at count 7).
153|- Explains why the newest, longest, most asset-heavy stages (Merge resolver
154|  with proof screenshots) interrupt while short stages complete.
155|
156|**Cons (against).**
157|- Proven for exactly one task-stage so far (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 5
158|  interrupts); the other 10 post-`finished` bare interrupts are unexamined.
159|- Cannot explain the 99 sub-15s interrupts (413 only happens at completion,
160|  minutes in).
161|- Backend 413 leaves no task-history trace of its own (the backend rejects
162|  before routing), so backend history alone can never confirm/deny further
163|  cases — runner journals are required.
164|

180|`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
181|residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then

185|generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).

180|`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
181|residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
182|re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
183|matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
184|is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
185|generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).
186|
187|**Pros (for).**
188|- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
189|  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
190|  11-20 (18).
191|- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
192|  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
193|  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
194|  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
195|- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
196|  (only uncaught fallible step there).
197|- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
198|  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.
199|
200|**Cons (against).**
201|- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
202|  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
203|  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
204|  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
205|- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
206|  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
207|  restart counters are unknown from here.
208|- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
209|  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.
210|
211|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
212|- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
213|  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`
214|  (12× local) — need the **local-alpha daemon journal on the backend host**
215|  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`, systemd user unit) for those windows: the
216|  `Runner failed: <message>` line names the fault, and restart-counter lines
217|  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.
218|- local-alpha build provenance: confirm it is also pre-11-21 (expected bare);
219|  after the 0.2.x rollout, bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should
220|  name this cause directly — re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
221|- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.
222|
223|### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run
224|
225|**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
226|failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
227|systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
228|progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
229|interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
230|remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
231|backend restart/502 window.
232|
233|**Pros (for).**
234|- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
235|  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
236|  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
237|  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
238|- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
239|  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`

=== fd5a74bf-7f95-413c-99d6-f8a12efb489b ===

title: Detect and surface runner rapid-restart (crash-loop) storms
goal: Case study task db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20: a hook-blocked recovery commit crashed the runner daemon on every poisoned-task claim and systemd restarted it 10,776 times before anyone noticed, because nothing tracks runner process restarts. Add restart-storm detection: have the runner send a per-process boot id with join and heartbeats, have the backend count distinct boot ids per runner in a sliding window, and when a runner exceeds a threshold (for example more than 5 boots in 10 minutes) mark it degraded or crash-looping in the runner fleet state, surface a banner in the runner UI, and emit a loud log; the flag clears when the runner stays up. Acceptance: backend tests prove the threshold trips and clears on synthetic heartbeat sequences; a runner test proves the boot id is stab

1|# Replicate & Test Guides — high level of task interruptions
2|
3|Task `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of
4|interruptions"). Companion to `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` (the wide-net cause
5|analysis). This folder turns each hypothesis from that analysis into a quick
6|guide: **how to recognise it, how to replicate or test it, and what is safe
7|to run versus what needs explicit permission first.**
8|
9|Screenshot reference: `assets/image.png` — task `7f6220c3` showing repeated
10|"Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and inflated
11|"Tried N times" badges (Merge resolver x6, Quick review x6, Automated tests
12|x10, In Progress x11).
13|
14|Scope note: this stage is **docs-only**. Every test below is a markdown
15|snippet for a follow-up code stage; no source or test files were added to the
16|repo. Run commands assume `node_modules` is installed (`npm install` in
17|`api/` and `frontend/`; runner tests need only Node's built-in runner).
18|
19|## Safety tiers used in every guide
20|
21|| Tier | Meaning | Examples |
22||---|---|---|
23|| **SAFE-LOCAL** | Runs entirely on this machine against temp dirs, in-memory Fastify (`app.inject`), or mock stores. No prod data, no agents, no network beyond localhost. | Unit tests for the ledger, scheduler, runner workdir cap, git-hook failure, 413 body limit |
24|| **PROD-READ-ONLY** | Reads production state (backend API `192.168.1.206:3100`, runner journals on the backend host or server2, worktrees `kb-<taskId>`). No writes, but still prod access. | Fleet-wide history recount, journal greps, worktree forensics |
25|| **PROD-ACTION** | Anything that invokes a real agent stage, restarts a runner/backend, reaps worktrees, or mutates task state. | Re-running `7f6220c3`'s Merge resolver, restarting `local-alpha`, manual resume of parked tasks |
26|
27|**Rule for this task:** SAFE-LOCAL guides may be run freely. Anything marked
28|PROD-READ-ONLY or PROD-ACTION is documented as a *procedure only* — **do not
29|execute it without explicit user permission**. Each such section is marked
30|`PROD-ONLY — DO NOT RUN WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION`.
31|
32|## Verdict table (cause -> guide -> replicability)
33|
34|| # | Cause (from WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md) | Guide | Verdict |
35||---|---|---|---|
36|| 1 | Worktree-cap exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap 5) | `GUIDE-01-worktree-cap-loop.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (runner `node:test` + api vitest) |
37|| 2 | HTTP 413 on `complete-execution` (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default) | `GUIDE-02-413-complete-payload.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (Fastify `inject`); real-task confirmation is PROD-READ-ONLY |
38|| 3 | local-alpha setup-phase deaths (bare, ~5 s, no `prompted`) | `GUIDE-03-local-alpha-setup-deaths.md` | PARTIAL locally (backend side simulatable); root cause PROD-READ-ONLY on the local-alpha host |
39|| 4 | Backend-unreachable / 502 crashing the daemon mid-run | `GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (localhost mock backend returning 502 / dropping); window-joining is PROD-READ-ONLY |
40|| 5 | Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks) | `GUIDE-05-commit-push-crash-loop.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (temp git repo + failing hook); real agent e2e is PROD-ACTION |
41|| 6 | Backend server restarts orphaning `running_*` tasks | `GUIDE-06-backend-restart-orphans.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (mock-store unit test of `reconcileInterruptedRuns`); fleet check PROD-READ-ONLY. Analysis: 0 occurrences observed — monitor only |
42|| A | Amplifier: Rule-0 instant re-dispatch, death counter counts cap refusals, "Tried N times" and the "after server restart" label | `GUIDE-07-amplifier-requeue-and-display.md` | REPLICABLE-LOCALLY (api + frontend unit tests) |
43|| T | Consolidated copy-paste test recipes and exact run commands | `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` | Reference |
44|
45|## How to read a guide
46|
47|Each guide has the same sections:
48|
49|1. **Signature** — what the flake looks like in the UI / task history / journals.
50|2. **Replicability verdict** — one of REPLICABLE-LOCALLY / PARTIAL / PROD-ONLY.
51|3. **Safe local replication** — steps + a TDD-style test example (red test first,
52|   then the code path that should satisfy it).
53|4. **Prod-only verification** (if any) — the exact commands that *would* be
54|   run on prod, clearly flagged, not to be executed without explicit user
55|   permission.
56|5. **Evidence to collect** — what to save if the issue is reproduced.
57|
58|## Test-run commands used throughout
59|
60|```bash
61|# api unit tests (vitest), from repo root:
62|cd api && npx vitest run flow/executionLedger.test.js        # single file
63|npm run test:api                                            # whole api suite
64|
65|# frontend unit tests (vitest):
66|cd frontend && npx vitest run src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js
67|
68|# runner unit tests (node:test, no deps beyond Node >= 20):
69|node --test runner/project.test.js
70|node --test runner/daemon.test.js
71|```
72|
73|New test files for these guides are **not** added in this docs-only stage;
74|`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` says exactly where each snippet would live. Note the
75|repo gate pins every `runner/*.test.js` in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`
76|(`buildBranches`), so a new runner suite file must also be registered there
77|in the code stage.
